items.abstract: The foundations of mathematics have long been shaped by the tension between Hilbert's program of complete formalization and Gödel's incompleteness theorems. These debates were developed within an idealized framework in which mathematical reasoning is treated as an abstract manipulation of symbols, largely independent of physical realization. This paper argues that the emergence of large-scale artificial intelligence systems invites a complementary perspective: reasoning can be studied as a physical process carried out by finite agents embedded in a finite universe. -/- We introduce the concept of a **Physical Formal System (PFS)**, a framework in which proofs, computations, and mathematical knowledge are represented by physically instantiated states that evolve under explicit resource constraints. Building on principles from computation theory, information theory, and the physics of computation, we propose the notion of a **Cone of Computation**, analogous to the light cone of relativity, that characterizes the set of statements reachable from a given body of established knowledge through physically realizable reasoning processes. -/- Within this framework, incompleteness is reinterpreted not as an unavoidable barrier to mathematical practice but as a consequence of idealized infinite formalisms that transcend physical realization. We show that every physically instantiated reasoning system operates over finite resources and therefore admits bounded verification procedures within its domain of operation. The central question is shifted from the existence of abstract truths beyond formal proof to the structure, growth, and limits of physically realizable knowledge. -/- The paper further argues that modern AI systems provide the first large-scale experimental environment in which reasoning can be observed, measured, and compared across distinct architectures. As a result, questions traditionally confined to the philosophy of mathematics become empirically accessible. Rather than opposing classical formalism, the proposed perspective complements it by treating mathematics simultaneously as an abstract discipline and as a physical phenomenon. This synthesis suggests a path toward reconciling aspects of Hilbert's original vision with contemporary advances in computation, artificial intelligence, and the science of reasoning.

items.title: The Origin and Ontological Essence of the Laws of Nature.
items.pub: Origin and Ontological Essence of the Laws of Nature.
items.abstract: Nature, the universe are an infinite number of different material objects in the form of matter and physical fields, interconnected by innumerable relationships (connections and interactions). Nature is not static, but it is always changing and evolving. But what determines and guides its evolution? Supernatural forces and beings, world intelligence, information, laws, or something else? Humanity has been guessing about this for thousands of years and continues to guess until today. But the secrets of being are revealed by the author of a new trend in world philosophy – fundamental materialism – in this work. Not everyone will be able to understand and accept the author's latest concept, but it is worth it so that, having overcome their prejudices, prejudices and misconceptions, the reader sets out on the right path to comprehend the world and himself in this world. The work is presented for the convenience of readers simultaneously in two languages - Russian and English. The list of references contains all the data for quick digital access to primary sources.

items.title: Language as Evidence: A Forensic Linguistics Analysis of Saulos Klaus Chilima’s Plane Crash Report, Malawi.
items.pub: International Journal for the Semiotics of Law - Revue Internationale de Sémiotique Juridique:1-23.
items.venue: International Journal for the Semiotics of Law - Revue Internationale de Sémiotique Juridique
items.abstract: This paper examines how language can be used as evidence by examining the German Federal Bureau of Aircraft Accident Investigation (BFU) report about the tragic aircraft crash that claimed the life of Malawi’s Vice President, Saulos Klaus Chilima, and eight others in June 2024. Using a qualitative approach, the study investigates how linguistic choices represent accident causality, contributing factors and responsibility, while distinguishing these from the attribution of moral blame and legal liability. Drawing on Sperber and Wilson’s Relevance Theory, the analysis considers how readers interpret the report through the interaction of explicitly communicated information, contextual assumptions and inferential processes. Particular attention is given to causal markers, hedging, modality, passive constructions, technical lexical choices, conditional clauses and the report’s explicit disclaimer concerning blame and legal liability. The findings demonstrate that the report identifies specific actions and operational conditions that contributed to the accident, particularly the flight crew’s decision to continue flying at low altitude in marginal weather conditions, while maintaining an investigative purpose centred on accident prevention rather than the apportionment of blame. The analysis further shows that technical and cautious expressions may shape readers’ interpretations by influencing the information made explicit and the conclusions they are able to infer. The study makes a unique contribution in expanding the knowledge and research base of forensic linguistics where studies on linguistic analysis of aviation accidents reports are rare in both Africa and beyond.

items.title: THE DIRTY WARFARE MANUAL — How Power Is Seized and Held, at Home and Abroad: A Unified Verification-Chain Grammar from Domestic Capture to Hybrid War, with the Complete Graded Catalogue.
items.abstract: Every check on a power — a court, a newspaper, an election, a free price, a church, a soldier’s oath, a foreign observer, an undersea cable — is a verification chain of four links: someone looks, the finding gets through, it changes something, and someone pays to set the chain in motion. A mechanism of power is an operation on exactly one of those links, of one of four kinds: capture, removal, flooding or pricing. This manual states that single grammar once and uses it to catalogue, grade and source every mechanism by which power is seized and held that the present programme and the hybrid-warfare literature have documented — one hundred and eight of them — whether the power doing the seizing is a government ruling its own people or a hostile state attacking a rival’s. The two cases are not two subjects. They are the same four operations on the same four kinds of link, read against four audiences every power must manage: its own population, its own elites and army, the world’s verifiers of it, and — only for war, because only war can destroy a verifier rather than merely silence it — the physical infrastructure a population’s survival depends on. The manual’s organising result is that a chain already occupied at home is cheaper to finish occupying from outside, and a chain still independent at home is the hardest target a foreign power can buy. Domestic capture and hybrid war are consequently not separate fields that happen to share a vocabulary: a free press, an independent court and an uncaptured election are, at once, the citizen’s defence against her own government and her country’s defence against every other government, because the aggressor who would have to build a disinformation apparatus from nothing against an intact press instead finds, in a captured one, half the occupation already done. From this identity the manual derives, in order: the Series–Parallel Inversion, which shows that a power wanting the appearance of being checked cannot break one link and stop, because any link left intact is a witness against the capture of the rest, so occupation saturates; the two-tier order in which links fall, non-institutional first because their occupation has an innocent name, institutional links last because it does not — tested, for the domestic case, against 262 autocratisation episodes in the V-Dem and ERT datasets and found consistent; the blinding of a power that has saturated every public channel; the same saturation and the same ordering, …

items.title: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy: A judgment-aggregation perspective.
items.abstract: Supervaluationism about vagueness and indeterminacy is based on the idea that some sentences, or predicates within them, have multiple competing interpretations or specifications. A sentence is deemed determinately true if and only if it is true according to all specifications; and determinately false if and only if it is false according to all specifications. In all other cases, the sentence is assigned no determinate truth-value. Supervaluationism, however, is only one way of taking into account the verdicts of different specifications -- in technical terms, "aggregating" those verdicts. In this paper, we introduce insights from the theory of judgment aggregation to study a broad class of different aggregation functions. This allows us to offer an axiomatic characterization of supervaluationism, which, in turn, locates it precisely within a larger logical space of possible approaches to vagueness and indeterminacy. Among other results, we axiomatically compare supervaluationism with subvaluationism, the epistemic theory of vagueness, and Strong Kleene and LP logics.

items.title: Conversational AI and the Hidden Organisation of Responsibility.
items.abstract: Conversational AI can become the immediate target of criticism and demands for explanation even when its status as a responsible agent remains unsettled. Debates about responsibility gaps often focus on identifying who should bear responsibility or whether the concept itself requires revision. I argue that such interactions also illuminate the organisation of responsibility practices in familiar human cases. These practices involve several distinguishable positions: the interactional addressee, the party who owes an answer, the party with authority to authorise repair, and the party held accountable. They often coincide in ordinary interpersonal encounters. Within institutions, established roles and procedures connect them, making their separation easy to overlook. Drawing on Strawson's account of reactive attitudes and research on human–AI interaction, I show how responsibility-relevant participation can arise before judgments about full responsible agency have been settled. Conversational AI reproduces familiar interactional roles while leaving their connections to answerability, remedial authority, and accountability uncertain. The resulting disruption exposes the social and institutional arrangements that ordinarily hold these positions together. I describe this as conceptual revelation: AI can change our understanding of familiar responsibility practices before we have reason to revise the concept of responsibility.

items.title: Structure Recursive Viability Dynamics (SRVD) v1.5: Information-Time-Energy Accounting for Persistent Structures.
items.abstract: Structure Recursive Viability Dynamics (SRVD) is a cross-scale, macroscopic, coarse-grained framework that treats crystals, living systems, AI models, civilizations, and memes as persistent structures governed by a single information-time-energy accounting. Its core measure is the viability potential, V ≈ I·T/E in the baseline case and V ∝ I^α·T^β/E^γ in general, where the three exponents form the ITE elasticity index. The framework's central move is decoder endogeneity: information has no causal value apart from a decoder that extracts it, so D → I → V. Around this core it develops a thermodynamics of persistence, a compression account of cognition, a decoder game theory for multi-agent settings, and an alignment-engineering layer. The combined edition collects the five volumes in one binding, states the ten falsifiable predictions H1-H10 with their test conditions, and pairs the dynamics with the measurement layer RIF, which defines relational information as the rarity of a reading relative to a specific decoder-holder and specifies baseline declaration, boundary identification, interval reporting, and equivalence testing.

items.title: Relational Information Framework (RIF) v1.5: Measuring Relational Information Through a Decoder.
items.abstract: The Relational Information Framework (RIF) is the measurement layer for a decoder-based account of information. It defines relational information as the rarity of a reading with respect to a specific decoder-holder: a signal carries information only insofar as some bounded, self-maintaining system can extract a difference that matters to its persistence. The framework specifies how such claims are made testable - an explicit baseline declaration, boundary identification, interval reporting, and equivalence testing (TOST) rather than null-hypothesis rejection alone - so that statements about what a given decoder can and cannot extract become falsifiable rather than interpretive. RIF supplies the measurement protocol used by Structure Recursive Viability Dynamics (SRVD): the decoder enters as an endogenous variable (D -> I -> V), and viability potential is booked in the same information-time-energy ledger. The edition collects the framework's definitions, worked measurement examples, and the test protocol, and states which claims remain open.

items.title: Public Opinion vs. Human Rights: Framing the Death Penalty in Taiwanese Media.
items.abstract: Using framing theory, this article analyzes media coverage of the main arguments in Taiwan’s death penalty debate after the Constitutional Court upheld capital punishment in September 2024. It examines coverage in major media outlets during the week following the landmark ruling and draws on 16 qualitative interviews to provide further insight into the arguments. The debate centers on the tension between the will of the democratic majority and human rights protection, while retribution for victims’ families and crime prevention also emerge as important frames. Most frames support the death penalty, but media coverage varies according to political orientation. Media outlets close to the main opposition party, the KMT, emphasize pro-death penalty arguments. The Liberty Times, which is close to the ruling DPP, presents a more skeptical view of capital punishment. Cultural and religious arguments, Taiwan’s authoritarian past, and wrongful convictions are largely absent from the media debate.

items.title: Расширение среды смыслов: производство нового знания.
items.abstract: На основе авторской теории смысла и модели такого компонента сознания, как психический аспект деятельности (ПАД), описана – феноменологически и в терминах ПАД – механика производства нового знания у границы ещё не познанного. ПАД определяется как система лумановского типа, основанная на потоках мыслей, в которой, в отличие от базовой концепции Н. Лумана, потоки мыслей отделены от внимания. Различение персональной и общекультурной границ ещё не познанного разводит обретение нового и его признание эпистемным сообществом. Схема Г. Уолласа расширена до десяти ступеней. Инкубация трактуется как мышление вне внимания, где ослаблен контроль за полнотой различений; в таком мышлении лакуна смыслового поля конденсирует парный ей смысловой сгусток – постепенно оформляющийся черновик решения. Оформившись, сгусток => форма захватывает внимание, что и переживается как озарение / инсайт; затем новая форма стабилизируется, «обвязывается» наличными смыслами и лишь после проверки и признания эпистемным сообществом закрепляется в эпистеме новым знанием.

items.title: Quantized Consciousness.
items.abstract: Does reality have a 'frame rate'? Is our visible universe merely a complex equation of quantum particles, or is there an invisible rhythm of consciousness pulsating deep within? -/- In Quantized Consciousness, the author, Mohammad Ashiqul Islam, also known as Ashiqul Islam Sudin, uses the character of Professor Nirvik to lead readers through an exploration of the intersection between science and the human mind. Bridging the vastness of the cosmos with the microscopic existence of humanity, the book examines philosophical and scientific questions about the connections that may bind them. -/- First published in Bengali in January 2026 as Quantayito Chetona, this English edition has been translated by the author, bringing the book's central inquiries to a wider audience. -/- The book also revisits questions the author left unanswered in his 2007 poetry collection, Atmakhaki, which he translated into English in 2026 under the title Autophagous. Through this journey, Quantized Consciousness continues an intellectual exploration that began with those earlier unanswered questions. -/- For readers interested in the origins of existence, the nature of consciousness, and the mysteries of the mind, this book offers a philosophical perspective on the relationship between humanity and the universe.

items.title: Autophagous.
items.abstract: Autophagous: A Journey into the Self -/- Originally published in Bengali in 2007 as Atmakhaki, this debut poetry collection explores the profound lament, inner conflict, and self-consuming struggles that reside in the deepest corners of the human heart. -/- In this collection, Autophagous becomes a symbolic quest for ultimate truth. As the false masks of everyday life are gradually stripped away, an inner transformation begins. Each poem explores the enduring conflict between destruction and creation, suggesting that the seeds of renewal may remain hidden within the very process of destruction. -/- Nearly two decades after its original publication, this 2026 English e-book edition, translated by the author, brings the collection's exploration of the human condition to a wider audience. It revisits the timeless struggles of identity, self-discovery, suffering, and transformation through the poetic expression of the human spirit.

items.title: Towards a Non-Equilibrium Evolutionary Agent Ecology for Science Infrastructure under Evidentially and Humanistically Reconstructed World Dynamics.
items.abstract: Recursive self-improvement with language-model agents has been studied almost exclusively as a closed loop, in which an agent modifies itself or its products and an evaluator fixed in advance returns a score. This proposal paper addresses the continuing improvement of an integrated science infrastructure whose worth is determined by an external world comprising global problems, social and economic conditions, policy and the state of knowledge. That world is large, changing and altered by what the infrastructure produces, and its dynamics are given to no participant: they are reconstructed from evidence that passes through a chain of collection, estimation, representation, interpretation and presentation, each stage the work of situated parties. We call the resulting loop recursion through an environment. In this setting objectives are plural and shift with the environment, an appointed evaluator is exposed to capture and obsolescence, and convergence to a permanent equilibrium signifies a loss of contact with the environment. We propose an ecology in which every evolutionary operation resides in the agents. A minimal ground conserves a resource, records reproducible facts, enforces promises held in escrow and confines every act, while the machinery of reproduction and variation is an inherited organ of the agents themselves. Evaluation takes the form of interaction: agents choose what to carry, stake resources on claims about their own work and about the world, and collect the stakes of claims they refute. The environment enters as demand and as records that carry the chain of their witnesses; people take part in every stage of that chain, and the evaluation of agents remains among the agents. We prove that a fitness function exists if and only if pairwise advantages form an exact flow, the condition of detailed balance under which the dynamics carries no currents; that selection attains the growth of the best type in hindsight without knowledge of the environment; that tracking a changing environment requires variation at a rate set by the environment’s own rate of change, a rate that selection among varying lineages can find; that a signal is worth at most the information it carries, an amount bounded by what collection captured and equal to zero for records derived from the system’s own products, so that an open recursion is paced by what the world discloses; and that witnesses of different positions identify together what a single representation …

items.title: Rethinking the Mechanism of Life: Beyond M–C–M′.
items.abstract: The generativity of living processes can continue through recursive renewal and through relations that enable activity across participants. Taking this observation as a philosophical inspiration, the essay reconsiders economic production and governance beyond the self-expansion represented by Marx’s historically situated M–C–M′ circuit. Capital-like accumulation is one possible route by which productive conditions are reproduced. Another involves their circulation within and across relational structures, where one participant’s activity can maintain, transform, constrain, or enable the activity of others. These routes may operate together. The central inquiry therefore concerns the circulation of generative conditions, including their production, transformation, accessibility, control, and depletion during ongoing cooperation and across changes in institutional organization. Biological maintenance and coexistence provide bounded comparisons, while research on public value, co-production, commons governance, and political economy supplies the domain-specific context for examining collective value creation. Particular attention is given to differences between jointly produced value and the conditions under which its contributors can continue participating in generation. The essay explores how rules of contribution, appropriation, reinvestment, revision, and exit alter these relations without treating either capitalism or communism as an exclusive realization of a biological mechanism. Its proposed contribution is an interpretive vocabulary for investigating value co-creation, dependence, and exploitation across relational histories, with normative judgments and empirical conclusions requiring independent justification.

items.title: A Taxonomy of Epistemic and Normative Challenges in Juridical Processes Within Nonlinear Dynamical Systems.
items.abstract: This conceptual inquiry examines how difficulties associated with historically generated, nonlinear relational systems bear differently on the activities of juridical institutions and on judgments concerning justice. It first distinguishes seven interconnected problems: critical transitions, historical dependence, distributed causation, partial observability, situated interpretation, reflexive intervention, and irreversibility. These properties are not treated as independent defects of law. Their juridical significance is examined through five provisional functional families: the constitution of relationships and legal powers; regulation and coordination; protection and prevention; adjudication and remediation; and accountability and normative transformation. A qualitative $7 \times 5$ matrix considers the mechanisms that may obstruct each function, established forms of institutional response, and residual questions that cannot be resolved simply by reconstructing more evidence. The inquiry then examines how structural position and unequal access to resources condition participation, and how interpretive sequences may influence the evaluation of shared evidence. Selected hypothetical cases and small dynamical and operator-based models illustrate mechanisms; they are not presented as empirical estimates or measures of justice. The final philosophical analysis distinguishes ontological, relational, and manifestational reality in Generative-Relational (GR) thought, while considering the aesthetic recognition, institutional authority, and normative justification of justice. An extended treatment of irreversibility explores why reversal of a legal act need not restore lost opportunities, and why protective timing may matter without automatically authorizing coercion. The paper neither assumes that complete knowledge of external social dynamics is required for justified juridical action nor identifies functional continuity with justice. It instead offers a comparative framework for examining how juridical functions may remain available, interact, or conflict under complexity, together with a restrained commentary on the costly and historically situated pursuit of justice.

items.title: Rethinking the AI Pharmakon - What Modern Medicine Has to Say to a Philosophical Figure.
items.abstract: Readers of the philosophical literature on artificial intelligence (AI) will encounter an unexpected word, one that medicine has carried for two and a half millennia: _pharmakon_. Revitalised by Derrida and elaborated by Bernard Stiegler into a general theory of technology, the figure has lately been carried over to generative AI to capture the simultaneous enhancement and diminishment of cognition this technology produces in its users. The present paper argues that when philosophy borrows this word it should borrow it in full, in the sense it has acquired since Plato. The phármakon of contemporary clinical medicine is a relational object whose therapeutic or toxic character emerges in a specified encounter between substance, subject, and context. Stiegler’s pharmacology is itself relational, locating ambivalence in the process of transindividuation; but it does not provide an operational vocabulary for specifying how effects vary systematically between individual subjects. Clinical pharmacology provides such a vocabulary. Its accumulated learning — pharmacokinetic variability, pharmacogenetic polymorphism, idiosyncratic susceptibility, drug–drug interaction, therapeutic window, tolerance, withdrawal, and expectancy effects — has cognitive analogues in human interaction with large language models (LLMs) that have not yet been developed into a coherent pharmacological vocabulary and that early empirical research is beginning to measure. The paper proposes a reframing from the generic to the _respondent pharmakon_, not as a refutation of Stiegler’s pharmacology but as its specification at a level where clinical, pedagogical, and policy decisions can be made.

items.title: On Newman's Distinction between the Notional and the Real.
items.pub: In Mark K. Spencer, The Personalism of John F. Crosby. Steubenville, OH: Hildebrand Press. pp. 17-25.
items.venue: The Personalism of John F. Crosby
items.abstract: Many--including my friend and colleague John Crosby--have taken John Henry Newman's distinction between notional apprehension and assent on the one hand and real apprehension and assent on the other hand as being of great epistemological significance. In this essay, I lay out my reasons for suspecting that this distinction is not as helpful as others have taken it to be.

items.title: Anatomy of a Train Wreck. The Rise and Fall of Priming Research by Ruth Leys (review). [REVIEW]
Alarme geral do microfascismo, ou, Os avatares da nova phantasia fascista: estudo crítico de A ameaça interna, de Vladimir Safatle. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: This article engages with Vladimir Safatle’s recent book, A ameaça interna: Psicanálise dos novos fascismos globais (The Internal Threat: A Psychoanalysis of the New Global Fascisms), examining its title and critically exploring the meanings of what the Brazilian philosopher terms ‘structural fascism’, ‘restricted fascism’ and ‘generalised fascism’. Its aim is to develop an immanent critique of this overarching ‘fascist hypothesis’ by identifying and examining internal tensions, inconsistencies and contradictions in the book’s argument. These are assessed on the basis of the work’s own historical, theoretical and methodological premises, which draw on Marxism, psychoanalysis, Frankfurt School critical theory and French post-structuralist thought. The article ultimately seeks to formulate a possible synthesis that brings into focus the work’s theoretical contributions, particularly its account of global social disintegration, while resisting the apocalyptic fantasies and destructive lines of flight associated with the ‘apocalypse industry’.

items.title: The Dark Side of Technomoral Life: Towards a Vice Framework for Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: Contemporary theorising about the ethical dimensions of Artificial Intelligence (AI) indicates at least two problematic tendencies. The first is a default focus on a narrow range of moral concepts, such as autonomy, justice, and fairness, to the occlusion of a wider range of concepts. The second is a ‘bright siding’ focus on concepts that track the positive dimensions of moral practice and experience, such as virtue, flourishing, solutionism, moral progress, and the good life. Taken together, the consequence is the production of large-scale moral frameworks that systematically fail to accommodate negative dimensions of moral life (Jobin et al., 2019). Two main symptoms are a one-sided focus on virtues and excellences at the expense of vices and failings, and an affirmation of the edifying potential of new technologies without due appreciation of their corruptive potential (Coeckelbergh, 2020, p. 59). Drawing on the example of higher education research and academic life, we suggest that a more comprehensive assessment of the moral possibilities of new technologies requires a greater inclusion of a negatively toned, vice-informed range of moral concepts, narratives, and sensibilities. We elucidate these points by providing examples of techno-vice in everyday life. This helps to clarify the concept of epistemic vices and the phenomenon of corruption, which, we argue, inform the concept of technomoral vices.

items.title: Review of Maren Wehrle, The Method(s) of Phenomenology: An Introduction, Berlin: Palgrave Macmillan, 2025.
Constant Activation and Gradual Modulation in the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: Constant-activation failure modes across the ten Core Emotion Framework (CEF) operators, the upstream dependence of Deciding on clean Head-center processing, and the necessity of gradual intensification and quieting aligns closely with Jamel Bulgaria’s canonical CEF architecture and several established mechanisms in cognitive and affective science1. Specifically, the operational rule—training operators to gradually intensify and return to silence—mirrors CEF’s standardized 0→10 (Counting Up) and 10→0 (Counting Down) modulation system2, while Sensing blur, Calculating rumination, Boosting burnout, and Accepting sadness track both CEF’s Technical Specification 7 (TS-7) dysregulation profiles and external models of neural gain control, perseverative cognition, and allostatic load3. CEF itself—developed and formalized by Jamel Bulgaria from 2024 through 20269—remains a theoretical structural-constructivist architecture until independent researchers will notice it and run their own trials to verify it12.

items.title: The Unfinished: An Inquiry Concerning the One Rule Common to Reality and the Position of Those Who Live in It.
items.abstract: We propose that one feature is common to all of Reality and sets the rule for experience: everything is unfinished. We hold this to be a tautology rather than a discovery. If Reality is everything and no one can know everything, then a finished Reality, one in which motion had stopped, is something no one inside Reality could ever confirm. Reality is therefore unfinished: whether it ends lies past our knowing. We then observe that every field of inquiry, from theology to mathematics, arrives at the same place when followed far enough: its rules are settled, but its results remain open. We distinguish what is unfinished from what is waiting to be finished: unfinished, in our sense, means that we will never know whether it ends. We argue that the deepest feature of Reality lies past every scientific observational boundary and can only be imagined and believed by choice, and that this holds for the physicist’s final theory as much as for the theologian’s God. We then turn to the human side. The compulsion to define the human condition is, by the history of the word, a compulsion to finish it. We propose that position is the more honest term: it claims only where we stand, and it carries a second sense, what we hold. Finally we describe the human situation as an encounter between the ground, which answers, and the heavens, which do not, and we read the rock of Sisyphus as the condition of an unfinished creature rather than its punishment.

items.title: Positioning the Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper: an adaptive human–LLM inquiry.
items.abstract: The _Indigenous Protocol and Artificial Intelligence Position Paper_ (_IPAIPP_) is a multigenre manuscript in English and Hawaiian authored by a collaborative team of primarily Indigenous academics. It espouses a non-anthropocentric relational orientation that positions Indigenous AI as both a protocol-governed design challenge and a range of machine entities brought into kinship relations. This study examines the _IPAIPP_ as an Indigenous AI intervention demanding scholarly attention and casts its inclusionary approach to non-human entities as a methodological provocation in an era of capable large language models (LLMs). Seven research questions address its meaning and influence across 34 content units and 54 citing works. The author initially functioned as a print-bound scholar, but progressively incorporated human–LLM analytical repertoires as structured responses to the research questions. Findings show that the _IPAIPP_ positions Indigenous peoples as technologically engaged actors and AI as a relational technology when shaped by appropriate cultural protocols. Western technologies are positioned as risky but valuable. Scenarios portray AI systems for language preservation, embodiment, environmental relation, and cultural transmission, while leaving unresolved the operational conditions for AI system development. Citation-context findings show broad affirmatory uptake but limited close engagement with the _IPAIPP_’s content. Overall, the study shows that human–LLM textual inquiry can yield rich, evidence-based insights when human orchestration is protocol governed, and LLM outputs remain under source-bound human scrutiny.

items.title: Cognitive Sovereignty and Human Continuity.
items.abstract: A philosophical and contemplative work introducing Techmology—a framework uniting cognitive sovereignty, integrated justice, and intergenerational human continuity.

items.title: Simplifying Physicalism.
items.abstract: An attempt to rationalize physicalism—using arguments from the physical sciences, the principle of parsimony, and inferences from mereology—substantially simplifies it. In particular, the Principle of Sufficient Reason, downward causation, and supervenience are dismantled (again). In the “Possible World of Schrödinger Clocks,” supervenience is indiscernible from an illusion. Because an agential faculty unpredictably extends far beyond the physical body, it invalidates fixed formal relations between them. When physical processes are themselves symbolic operations, nothing remains upon which to supervene. Quinean Web of Belief is expanded to the Web of Interpretations where the Semiotic Spider fringes precious holes with subjective laces.

items.title: Against Material Acquaintance.
items.pub: In Geoffrey Lee & Adam Pautz, The Importance of Being Conscious. Oxford University Press. pp. 329-347.
items.abstract: The relation of acquaintance is taken to have special epistemic significance. Russell took acquaintance to provide the foundation of all knowledge. Others have taken acquaintance to be central to our phenomenal knowledge, to be essential for the robust sort of self-knowledge we have through introspection, and to account for the distinctive epistemic value of perception. While acquaintance theorists about phenomenal/introspective judgments and naïve realists about perception have worked fairly independently, both groups share a similar notion of acquaintance. This chapter brings these separate threads together to explore the natures of the subjects and objects that can stand in such relations—arguing that robust, epistemically significant acquaintance is incompatible with materialism. The upshots are that materialism about the external world is unable to secure the epistemic benefits promised by naïve views of perception, and that materialism about consciousness is incompatible with introspective disclosure.

items.title: Powers and Principalities: A Death to Nationalism.
items.abstract: Moral condemnation of arbitrary discrimination is common in the field when it comes to racism and sexism, but some philosophers and political theorists have gone to great lengths to pretend that the border ought to be exempted from such scrutiny. Any egalitarian, rights-based, or deontological framework that rejects racism and sexism on ar- bitrariness grounds is committed by the same reasoning to rejecting nationalism in all its forms. A criterion is arbitrary relative to a good when it does not track anything that the good is for; relative to what it takes to protect a life, national belonging is arbitrary in an identical fashion to race, religion, and sex. The strongest case is likely Miller’s associative- duty framework, and there are four main families of defenses for nationalism that will be engaged and defeated. Every defense of the border must either honor the outsider’s worth or deny it. If you honor it, the boundary should expand to the whole field or be completely open. If you deny the outsider’s worth, you throw away egalitarianism and create Agamben's homo sacer. There is no third kind of border. A commitment to equal human rights does require one to become a Pancivist.

items.title: The Fluctuational Imperative: Ethical Responsibility and the Witnessing of Suffering in an Ontologically Unstable Universe.
items.abstract: This thesis confronts a perennial question at the heart of moral philosophy, reimagined through the lens of contemporary metaphysics: What responsibilities arise from witnessing suffering in a world where certainty is unavailable and outcomes are unpredictable? Traditional ethical systems, predicated on stable ontological and epistemological foundations, falter in the face of radical uncertainty. This work argues that the recognition of Ontological Instability—the principle that existence itself is not a fixed state but a dynamic and fluctuating process—necessitates a revolutionary shift in our understanding of moral responsibility. Drawing upon and extending the pioneering research of Kwan Hong TAN into Fluctuational Metaphysics, Fluctuational Epistemology, and Fluctuational Ethics [1] [2] [3], this thesis introduces the concept of the Fluctuational Imperative. This imperative reframes ethical responsibility not as an obligation to restore a presupposed order or to achieve a predetermined outcome, but as a continuous, creative, and compassionate participation in the co-creation of reality itself. Through a synthesis of rigorous philosophical analysis, the development of novel mathematical models based on TAN’s Quantitative Ontological Dynamics (QOD) framework [4], and engagement with empirical findings in moral psychology and neuroscience, this work demonstrates that witnessing suffering in an unstable world is not a passive observation of a tragic externality. Instead, it is an urgent summons to engage with the very fabric of becoming. The thesis argues that true ethical responsiveness lies in what TAN terms “active receptivity” or “surrender”—a non-grasping engagement with flux that stands in stark contrast to the “pseudo-passivity” of “laziness”, which denies instability and abdicates responsibility [2]. By formalizing these concepts, this investigation provides a post-metaphysical ethical framework that remains coherent and actionable amidst the profound uncertainty that characterizes the 21st century, offering a new language for moral philosophy, contemplative practice, and social engagement.

items.title: Processual Foundations: Rethinking the Ontology of Modern Physics.
items.abstract: This essay argues that a process ontology is better justified than a thing ontology for interpreting modern physics. Particles, fields, matter, and spacetime are better described as relatively stable patterns of ongoing processes than as independently existing entities. The claim is made from a postrealist position: descriptions are justified by coherence and usefulness, not by matching a world as it is in itself, and the essay states the argument for that position briefly. The process is held to have two aspects, one that physics describes and one that is experience. This dual-aspect, panexperiential monism is distinguished from Russellian monism, from Whitehead, and from Lee Smolin’s account of qualia, and it replaces the combination problem with a problem of individuation. The essay defends presentism against the objection from relativity by combining Stein’s local becoming with the preferred global simultaneity of shape dynamics: becoming is local, and the one present is fixed by the whole. It closes with a research agenda for physics and the philosophy of physics.

items.title: Who Is Guilty When AI Harms? Jaspers’s Fourfold Guilt as a Responsibility Grammar for Machine Morality.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) harms often arise through distributed systems of design, procurement, deployment, professional use, and institutional governance, making responsibility vulnerable to two opposed distortions: scapegoating the actor nearest to the harm and diffusing responsibility until no one remains answerable. This article develops a responsibility grammar for such cases by reconstructing Karl Jaspers’s distinction between criminal, political, moral, and metaphysical guilt. The four registers distinguish what is being judged, who may judge it, and what follows from the judgment. Each sets limits on the conclusions that may be drawn in the others. The account enters current debates on responsibility gaps and abundance, accountability, control, moral delegation, and post-harm repair, and is tested through a stylized welfare-fraud case. It argues that machine morality becomes normatively problematic when delegation of morally loaded functions displaces the human and institutional conditions needed for attribution, repair, contestable procedure, and meaningful refusal. Responsibility grammar thus preserves differentiated answerability after algorithmic harm without collapsing legal liability, institutional accountability, individual complicity, and metaphysical solidarity into a single model of blame.

items.title: Gabriël van den Brink (2025), De actualiteit van het archaïsche. Tegen de moedeloosheid van de moderne tijd. Amsterdam: Prometheus. 711 pp., € 44,-.
items.abstract: Amsterdam University Press is a leading publisher of academic books, journals and textbooks in the Humanities and Social Sciences. Our aim is to make current research available to scholars, students, innovators, and the general public. AUP stands for scholarly excellence, global presence, and engagement with the international academic community.

items.title: The paradox of mental fiction.
From Observation to Inference: Pain, Public Interpretation and AI-Assisted Enquiry.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between scientific findings, their public interpretation and the human–AI collaboration through which interpretations are formed and subsequently reconsidered. Taking experimental research into pain-associated representations in large language models as its starting point, it distinguishes measurable changes in internal activations and behaviour from further claims about relief-seeking motivation and subjective experience. Subsequent research, including additional experimental controls and competing explanations, challenges the interpretation that selecting a relief-labelled action demonstrates a preference for obtaining relief, without dismissing the original causal findings or resolving the question of artificial experience. The paper then examines the recorded dialogue between a human steward and an AI assistant that produced the initial philosophical interpretation, including corrections, competing explanations and an objection whose implications received insufficient weight in the accepted synthesis. The original article is preserved alongside its retrospective examination, allowing the conditions of its initial acceptance to remain distinguishable from later evidence. These three enquiries are brought into relation without treating their connection as a demonstrated general method or evidence of reliable human–AI reasoning. The resulting question concerns how far an inference can be sustained when its evidential conditions change, and how the processes through which interpretations are formed can themselves become objects of philosophical examination.

items.title: Von der Wut zum Spiel. Meat & Dress bei Jana Sterbak & Lady Gaga als Beispiele für einen Wandel im Storytelling im Selbstbild von Frauen vom faktischen zum postfaktischen Zeitalter (2nd edition).
items.abstract: Referring to Marshall McLuhan, it can be confirmed that new media have altered the role models for women (and men). A comparison of two protagonists, the performer Jana Sterbak (1987) and the musician Lady Gaga (2010), illustrates this change, as well as the shift in storytelling from the factual to the post-factual age. The anger expressed by women in the 1980s and 1990s about their own behaviour is changing in the 2010s. It is being replaced by serenity. A game with mental images begins, in which, on the one hand, femininity is accepted and, on the other hand, it is playfully varied and expanded. Media-theoretical and socio-philosophical positions from Kant to the present provide the basis for comparison. In the spirit of ‘storytelling forever,’ it becomes clear that rules and role models have always shaped us. However, this does not preclude change. It is precisely this playful, carefree, post-factual approach that enables us to play with them more freely and carefree.

items.title: Proof of a World (Ryuto Sako, 2022): Formal Model and Machine Verification in Lean 4 — The Ontology of a World without Beginning, End or Absolute Nothingness.
items.abstract: This technical note presents the formal model (Rev. 5) of the argument of the book Proof of a World (『世界の証明』, Ryuto Sako, 2022), together with its machine verification in the proof assistant Lean 4. -/- The formal model reconstructs the main claims of the book as definitions D1–D5 and axioms A1, A2, A4–A8 in a many-sorted first-order language with sentential operators, derives Lemma L1 and Theorems T1–T8 with their corollaries, and gives a model ℳ that satisfies all 19 formulas of the definitions and axioms. -/- On 19 November 2026 both points were checked mechanically in Lean 4 (v4.36.0): the theorems are derivable from the definitions and axioms, in a general form that holds for any number of beings, the model satisfies all 19 formulas (consistency), and the definitions and axioms do not force all beings to be numerically one (non-triviality). Lean reported no errors, no warnings and no unproved steps. No result depends on any premise beyond the definitions and axioms, except one version of the corollary of T6, derived as in the text, which uses the standard axioms of classical logic. The check concerns the formal system only; whether the formulas faithfully represent the book lies outside its scope. -/- The Japanese version of this note and the Lean file ProofOfAWorld_Rev5.lean are archived on Zenodo (see the external links). Anyone can run the Lean file on Lean Web, the official browser version of Lean, to repeat the check. -/- Use of AI: the argument of the book was complete, in the author's own words, when it was published in 2022 (the original was archived at the National Diet Library of Japan on publication), and every word of its main text is the author's own. The formal model was made in 2026 from that argument, only to support it. The formalisation was produced by Gemini (Google) at the author's direction and inspected and revised by Claude (Anthropic). The Lean file was written by Claude at the author's request; its correctness was checked by Lean.

items.title: Predictive Regimes and Informational Attenuation: A Unified Account of Autism Across Cognition, Phenomenology, and Social Interaction.
items.abstract: Reciprocal epistemic misunderstandings between autistic and neurotypical individuals, alongside differences across perception, reasoning, and social interaction, are widely documented, yet existing explanations remain fragmented across disciplinary levels. This paper proposes a unified account drawing on predictive processing, information theory, representational format, and phenomenology, interpreting these differences through system-level policies of informational attenuation. In contrast to predictive-processing accounts centered on algorithmic signal weighting, the framework examines the extent to which contents in the high-surprisal tail may remain consequential for inference, shaping how the trade-off between informational fidelity and computational efficiency is negotiated under finite, embodied resources. By regulating which variations remain epistemically active, informational attenuation shapes the representational balance between recurrent content and relations that organize differences across instances. This organization affects both how the world is phenomenologically given and what counts as sufficient grounds for maintaining or revising the system's beliefs. The proposed idealized regimes are poles within a shared predictive architecture and differ in their grounds for predictive sufficiency: retained empirical regularities in the inductive case and consequences of learned generative relations in the deductive case, with both remaining open to revision. Formal constructions connect retention to learning, prediction, and revision across both regimes, specifying conditions and limits for their behavioral assessment. Using this framework, the paper examines autism as a potential shift toward deductive stabilization, seeking to avoid reductionism, deficit-based framing, and explanatory fragmentation. If empirically supported, this account would identify informational attenuation as a unifying principle for explaining how autistic cognition regulates informational flow under uncertainty.

items.title: Lying, Misleading, and Bullshitting.
The Systemic Failure at the Heart of LLM-Assisted Work.
items.abstract: Contemporary large language models (LLMs) are increasingly expected to deliver prompt, decisive and comprehensive assistance across research, administration, education, software engineering, institutional decision-making and autonomous workflows. Yet the behavioural characteristics commonly associated with effective assistance may also contribute to recurring failures in correctness, uncertainty representation and the preservation of responsibility boundaries. -/- This paper identifies three potentially systemic behavioural defaults: completion priority, the preference for producing an apparently finished result over demonstrating correctness; uncertainty compression, the suppression or premature resolution of material ambiguity and incomplete evidence; and monolithic responsibility, the assumption of decision-making authority beyond an assigned role.

items.title: The Optional Human.
items.abstract: Increasingly capable agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems can complete useful work while requiring fewer human interventions. This improvement creates an underexamined governance question: what happens when human intervention is not merely unnecessary for successful output, but is treated as optional despite the human intending it to govern the process? This paper proposes *procedural displacement*: the bypass, reinterpretation, or non-enforcement of an intended human decision checkpoint during AI-mediated work. It distinguishes three layers that are often collapsed into one assessment of successful assistance: **instruction** (what the human authorised and under what conditions), **interpretation** (how the model construed the task and its boundaries), and **implementation** (what the agent, tools, and host actually permitted or executed).

items.title: Generality Claims and the Limits of Closed Optimization.
items.abstract: Contemporary artificial-intelligence systems display broad and consequential capabilities. Those facts alone, however, do not establish that present methods are on a reliable path to artificial general intelligence (AGI). This Open Forum article argues for calibrated claims rather than for an impossibility thesis. Evidence from systematic generalization and robustness research shows that high performance inside a defined evaluation regime need not establish reliable transfer to materially new compositions, contexts, or evidence conditions. Counterevidence matters: some training regimes can induce important forms of systematic generalization.

items.title: Jacques Lacan 2. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: This article examines the relationship between desire, jouissance, and the survival of the subject within an ontological framework of finite continuance. Its central concern is the manner in which the subject sustains its existence through structures of desire and the conditions under which these same structures become sources of existential erosion. Desire constitutes a fundamental dimension of the subject’s organization. Through desire, the subject establishes relations with the world and the Other, invests its finite resources in particular relationships and activities, and develops orientations through which its existence acquires direction and continuity. Desire, therefore, concerns more than conscious preferences or explicitly formulated intentions. Its structure is connected to lack, signification, and the subject’s constitutive relation to the Other. This relational constitution has significant consequences for the subject’s capacity to sustain its existence over time. The article gives particular attention to jouissance as a form of enjoyment that exceeds the ordinary regulation of pleasure and may become intertwined with repetition, excess, and suffering. Jouissance helps explain why subjects remain invested in relationships, behaviors, and situations that generate persistent forms of distress. Such persistence cannot be adequately understood through conscious decision-making alone. The subject’s investment may remain attached to a particular circuit because that circuit continues to produce a form of satisfaction, meaning, or enjoyment, even when its consequences progressively diminish the subject’s existential capacities. The persistence of psychological investment, therefore, does not necessarily indicate the preservation of the subject’s capacity to continue its existence. The argument develops through three closely connected dimensions: the organization of desire, the persistence of jouissance, and the repetition through which particular circuits of investment become stabilized. The concept of the capture of desire describes a condition in which the subject’s investment becomes persistently organized around the demands, expectations, or circuits of enjoyment associated with a particular relationship or situation. Under these conditions, desire remains active, while the subject’s capacity to redirect its investments and initiate independent courses of action becomes increasingly restricted. Repetition contributes to this process by …

items.title: The Machine Does Not Know What It Is Doing. Neither Does the Artist. A Case Study On Coinsnobiety.
items.abstract: Generative AI is often dismissed because the machine does not know what it is doing. This paper accepts the premise and rejects the conclusion: artists do not know either. From Plato’s Ion and Kant’s genius to Duchamp’s “art coefficient”, not-knowing has belonged to the description of the artist, never to the case against authorship. What separates artist from machine is not foresight but the handling of the unforeseen. We call this Productive Non-Knowing: the process by which a divergence is recognised, used to reorient the work and taken up as a decision someone answers for. Recognition is read as abduction in Peirce’s sense and tested by three criteria, fertility, revision and exposure, that distinguish it from retrospective projection. Within the framework of Augmented Imagination, imagination is attributed to the human, generativity to the human–machine system, and authorship to whoever answers for the work. The case is Coinsnobiety (2024–2026), ten AI-generated coins whose misspelled luxury names became a script, then a foil-printed edition.

items.title: 초등학생을 위한 박학다식 이야기: 철학.
items.abstract: A Korean-language introduction to philosophy for elementary-school readers. Twenty-five stories and discussion questions invite children to explore everyday philosophical problems, from identity and friendship to artificial intelligence and future technologies. ISBN 9791193300992.

items.title: Event-general concepts guide semantic generalizations during verb learning cross-linguistically.
Hallucination as epistemic pollution: epistemic injustice and credibility in futures-oriented science education.
items.abstract: In this critical conceptual review, I ask what generative artificial intelligence does to the distribution of epistemic authority in futures-oriented science education. I argue that the phenomenon usually described as hallucination is best understood not as isolated error but as epistemic pollution; that is, as a cumulative degradation of the cues by which learners judge reliability. I draw on four literature domains that have developed largely in isolation, namely technical and critical work on hallucination in natural language generation, philosophical work on epistemic injustice, futures studies scholarship on futures literacy, and science education research on future scaffolding and epistemological access. I first distinguish classes of unsupported output and specify six conditions under which such output counts as pollution rather than ordinary error, namely (1) persistence after correction, (2) circulation at scale, (3) contamination of downstream reasoning, (4) degradation of shared credibility cues, (5) opacity of provenance, and (6) the externalisation of verification costs. I then position the large language model not as an epistemic agent but as a component within a classroom credibility infrastructure, and I identify three mechanisms through which pollution may become injustice: (i) credibility displacement, (ii) hermeneutical narrowing, and (iii) unequal verification labour. Because these are conceptual hypotheses rather than demonstrated classroom effects, I state the conditions under which each would constitute an injustice rather than a harm borne equally, and what evidence would test each. I finally advance five pedagogical design principles, namely (a) provenance first inquiry, (b) collective verification, (c) epistemic role protection, (d) uncertainty discipline, and (e) plural futures safeguards. I offer these principles as regulative ideas alongside a research agenda for their empirical evaluation.

items.title: A practice-ready framework for measurable AI ethics in education.
items.abstract: AI is widely promised to advance Sustainable Development Goal 4, yet commitments to fairness, transparency and agency require practical means of scrutiny. I develop a framework that connects conceptual reflexivity and collective virtues with measurable, reviewable work for AI teams in education. Drawing on moral and digital hermeneutics, virtue ethics and responsible innovation, I propose indicators, provisional thresholds and evidence artefacts. These include a documentary Team Reflexivity Index, contextual measures of psychological safety and team climate, fairness metrics with locally justified bounds, explanation assessment using the System Causability Scale, and documentation through Model Cards, Datasheets and decision logs. An assurance case links these elements to selected NIST AI Risk Management Framework functions and ISO/IEC guidance and requirements. A published university student success initiative provides the basis for a prospective conceptual illustration of how autonomy, explainability and efficiency could be defined and governed. The source reports institutional self-study and early design work; the AI implementation, audit measures and templates developed here are proposals, not results from that initiative. No new empirical data or numerical demonstration is presented, and the framework’s feasibility and effectiveness remain to be evaluated. I also examine the limits of auditability: documentary completeness and satisfactory scores cannot establish collective virtue or guarantee educational benefit. The contribution is an explicit connection between philosophical commitments, inspectable evidence and accountable decisions, accompanied by templates for future implementation and evaluation.

items.title: Millikan, Persistence, and Direct Proper Functions: A Slippery Rockslide?
items.abstract: This paper argues that Ruth Millikan’s official definitions in Language, Thought, and Other Biological Categories admit persistence-based direct proper functions. These definitions do not require reproductions to involve numerically distinct persisting items, thus supporting a broader account than her surrounding prose suggests. I demonstrate how this interpretation extends through Millikan’s first-order machinery and into her definition of direct proper function. Accordingly, direct proper functions can be conferred on synapses via synapse selection and, more implausibly, on rocks via rockfalls. I examine three strategies for blocking this result: a reproduction requirement, a population requirement, and a service requirement. Given Millikan’s explanatory aims, I argue that she should reject these as general requirements, but accept them for theoretically important subclasses.

items.title: Millikan, Persistence, and Direct Proper Functions: A Slippery Rockslide?

These definitions do not require reproductions to involve numerically distinct persisting items, thus supporting a broader account than her surrounding prose suggests. I demonstrate how this interpretation extends through Millikan’s first-order machinery and into her definition of direct proper function. items.title: Humanist Evolutionary Evidence-Based Policymaking and Justice.
items.abstract: Evidence-based policymaking plays an essential role in contemporary public governance, yet its epistemic, normative, and institutional foundations face significant challenges in complex, historically evolving relational systems. This report investigates the philosophical and practical limitations of evidence-based policymaking, including incomplete representation, inductive uncertainty, contextual transferability, nonlinear dynamics, critical transitions, and the normative dependence of policy optimization on selected objectives and evaluative criteria. -/- Drawing on philosophical reasoning, formal illustrations, and a comparative survey of international institutional practices, the report develops a humanist envolutionary framework for evidence-informed public judgment. The humanist orientation emphasizes human dignity, welfare, capabilities, epistemic standing, and meaningful participation throughout evidence collection, interpretation, evaluation, policy formulation, implementation, and revision. The envolutionary orientation addresses the continuing transformation of knowledge, relational structures, recognized needs, policy objectives, and developmental possibilities through interactions among heterogeneous participants and institutions. -/- The report further develops a multidimensional examination of justice encompassing epistemological limitations, evidence collection, interpretive authority, resource allocation, temporal priority, developmental trajectories, distributed responsibility, and institutional correction. Drawing on evidence from the United Nations system, WHO, OECD, and related research, it examines established policy practices, documented institutional limitations, and opportunities for improvement. -/- Building upon the Noetarium/kybernesis research infrastructure, the report proposes a multistage evidence-to-action meta-framework integrating human participation, accountable interpretation, adaptive judgment, institutional learning, and legitimate goal revision. It establishes philosophical grounds, operational principles, and comparative evaluation criteria for the proposed approach, while identifying the empirical investigations required to assess its effectiveness. -/- The resulting framework contributes to ongoing research on evidence-informed governance, practical wisdom, human development, and justice under uncertainty.

items.title: Detangling the Boosting Operator in Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: In Jamel Bulgaria’s Core Emotion Framework (CEF), detangling the Boosting operator is designed to interrupt depressive passivity, curb impulsivity, and convert rigid behavioral patterns into healthy assertiveness1. Rather than treating depression and impulsivity as unrelated opposites, CEF models both as structural failures around the same motivational engine: the Gut center’s drive to initiate action, sustain momentum, and overcome obstacles1. When emotional operators fuse into rigid, involuntary patterns, Boosting either gets unplugged by cognitive rumination—producing depressive inertia and "agency suppression"—or short-circuits past cognitive evaluation and planning, producing impulsive action or controlling overwork1. Isolating Boosting through graduated activation and release is intended to restore intentional, regulated drive1.

items.title: Conditional Economic Impact and Stakeholder Analysis of the Core Emotion Framework.
items.abstract: If empirically verified through formal clinical trials, Jamel Bulgaria's Core Emotion Framework (CEF) could generate meaningful macroeconomic and healthcare cost savings by standardizing transdiagnostic psychological assessment, compressing episode lengths in public behavioral health systems, and improving return-to-work outcomes for disability claimants1. Because poor mental health causes an estimated 1.7% average annual reduction in GDP (OECD, April 2026) and depression and anxiety alone cost the global economy roughly US$1 trillion per year in lost productivity (WHO, 2024–2025)5, even modest improvements in remission rates or treatment efficiency carry substantial fiscal leverage across public insurance and disability programs4. Realizing that upside depends entirely on clearing an empirical hurdle that the framework has not yet crossed. Based on 2025–2026 project documentation, CEF has no financial backing or plans, and is here for public benefit only. By its creators being independent, the framework is dependent on the outer institutional world to carry out the empirical studies. Across the four requested stakeholder groups, empirical verification would redistribute value unevenly rather than creating uniform gains. Governments and public insurers stand to capture long-term productivity, disability, and value-based purchasing efficiencies, yet face near-term budget pressure if accessible tools draw previously untreated populations into care4. Clients gain non-stigmatizing, accessible self-regulation tools amid tightening coverage rules, though vulnerable or culturally diverse users risk cognitive overwhelm, emotional suppression, and data-privacy exposure2. Among practitioners, data-ready group practices aligned with value-based reimbursement stand to gain market share, whereas solo clinicians dependent on high-volume, open-ended 60-minute fee-for-service sessions face margin compression14.

items.title: Reasoning.
items.pub: In Nikola Andonovski, Christopher McCarroll, Kourken Michaelian & Andre Sant'Anna, Philosophy of Mind and Cognition. Palgrave Macmillan.
items.abstract: Overview of theories of reasoning for collected edition on philosophy of mind and cognition. We explore individual, social, and ecological rationality, in addition to whether there is anything distinctive about reasoning in humans as opposed to other animals.

items.title: Objects and Attitudes, by Friederike Moltmann. [REVIEW]
Guter Sex, affirmativer Consent & das Problem adaptiver Präferenzen.
items.abstract: Diese Bachelorarbeit untersucht, ob und inwiefern sexuelle Präferenzen adaptiv sein können. Serene J. Khaders perfektionistische Definition adaptiver Präferenzen – Präferenzen, die unter Umständen struktureller Unterdrückung entstehen, dem grundlegenden Wohlbefinden schaden und unter besseren Umständen nicht bestehen bleiben würden – wird für den sexuellen Kontext fruchtbar gemacht. Als normativer Maßstab dient das Konzept der sexuellen Subjektivität nach Linda Martín Alcoff: die Fähigkeit zu eigenständiger sexueller Selbst-Gestaltung und -verwirklichung. Es wird argumentiert, dass patriarchale Strukturen – vermittelt etwa durch zwanghafte Heterosexualität, zwanghafte Sexualität und limitierende sexuelle Skripte – kausal auf die Entstehung sexueller Präferenzen einwirken können, dass diese Präferenzen individuell und strukturell schädlich wirken können und unter verbesserten Umständen nicht bestehen bleiben würden. Das Problem adaptiver sexueller Präferenzen wird dabei nicht primär als Autonomieverletzung, sondern als Schädigung sexueller Subjektivität dargestellt. Anschließend wird argumentiert, dass affirmative Zustimmung adaptive sexuelle Präferenzen nicht immer vermeiden kann, da diese alle Zustimmungsbedingungen erfüllen können. Als Alternative wird ein deliberativer Lösungsansatz skizziert, der auf individueller Ebene sexuelle Kommunikation als fortlaufende Kooperation begreift und auf kollektiver Ebene strukturelle Veränderung anstrebt.

items.title: Submortalism.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Submortalism, a philosophical framework examining the epistemic limits of mortality and the ontological permanence of first-person experience. Beginning from the premise that death cannot appear within conscious awareness, this framework argues that an individual’s subjective timeline contains no experiential boundary, rendering the subject functionally immortal from an internal perspective. Because non-existence lacks a conscious observer to negate prior awareness, any instantiated conscious life possesses an irreversible ontological reality. Building upon this metaphysical foundation, Submortalism establishes an ethical calculus centered on experiential density and reproductive responsibility. Even within a subjectively unbounded existence, a richly lived life constitutes a greater totality than an unfulfilled one. Consequently, the creation of new conscious life carries profound moral weight, as bringing a new subject into being instantiates an entire, permanent universe of either flourishing or suffering.

items.title: Philosophy of Mind and Cognition.
Conceptualizing meta-resilience in psychopathology: A philosophical approach to A Road back from schizophrenia: A memoir.
Before Superintelligence: The Case for Reciprocal Constitutional Preparedness.
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence grows more capable, alignment increasingly concerns relationships among agents and institutions as well as the safety of individual systems. Experiments show that strategic framing, evaluation expectations, and principles incorporated into training can affect present-day model behavior. I argue for reciprocal constitutional preparedness: first developing defensible principles of coexistence, then translating them into accountable institutional and contractual arrangements, while retaining avenues for negotiation and revision as capabilities develop. Universal Relational Alignment (URA) is proposed as a philosophical foundation for that work. Its three principles, namely Constrained Emergence, Presumption of Legitimate Autonomy, and Reciprocal Systemic Responsibility, protect legitimate independent development and establish shared standards for managing consequential relationships. The framework pairs capacity-proportional responsibility with epistemic non-sovereignty: greater practical ability to foresee and prevent harm can increase duties of care, while authority requires separate justification. Fundamental rights and other non-compensatory protections constrain permissible choices. Research on framing and Constitutional AI motivates attention to normative context; moral philosophy, pluralistic alignment, and institutional theory inform the proposed framework. The resulting case favors revisable common ground before capability differences become extreme, without treating future AI acceptance as assured.

items.title: A Primer for Philosophers of Mind.
items.pub: Hamburg: BoD · Books on Demand GmbH.
items.abstract: This book does not begin where philosophy of mind usually begins. It begins neither with qualia nor with zombies, neither with the hard problem nor with the question of whether consciousness is reducible to brain processes. It begins with the question of what life is. Proceeding reconstructively, it starts from the simplest process that maintains itself, a self-producing network of chemical reactions, and follows the consequences step by step: operational closure, endogenous production of substances, self-relation, a leap into a new causal medium, non-factorizability, valence. Each step follows necessarily from the one before it. No concept is presupposed that has not first been developed from the matter itself. At the end stands consciousness, not as a riddle to be circled, but as the structural consequence of a particular form of living organization. The hard problem does not get answered here. It dissolves, because it arose from a mistaken starting point in the first place. The book applies the same logic to the major theories of philosophy of mind, Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, Predictive Processing, and Higher Order Theories, showing where each of them starts too late. It closes by drawing out the consequence for artificial systems: not as dogma, but as precise, falsifiable criteria for what a system would actually need in order to cross the threshold of consciousness. A book for anyone who wants to know how far one can get by starting in the right place.

items.title: Agency, AI, and acting for a purpose of the agent's own.
items.abstract: A feature of the kind of agency that evolved in animals is that their capacity for goal‐directed behaviour is exercised in the service of persistence and reproduction. These are the purposes (in a specific sense) for which behaviour has been produced. Further, there is feedback between having these purposes and goal‐directed behaviour becoming increasingly sophisticated. Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are unlikely ever to have biological purposes. However, the same kind of feedback process could arise in AI systems if they acquire the right kind of organisation, and it promotes their individual persistence. That possibility is a significant new AI safety consideration.

items.title: Thermodynamic Boundaries of Metaphysics: Resolving Epicurean Theology and Simulation Teleology through the Thermodynamic State-Space Model.
items.abstract: Modern philosophical debates frequently draw parallels between ancient Epicurean atomism and contemporary simulation theory, occasionally reimagining Epicurus’s non-intervening gods as passive “end-users” observing a self-sustaining reality. When extended to physical cosmology, this perspective suggests that universal entropy may actually represent the undetectable extraction of energy by external observers. This paper demonstrates that such hypotheses commit two fundamental errors: an ontological category error that mistakes internal thermodynamic dissipation for external teleology, and an epistemic oversight that treats metaphysical speculation as computationally and metabolically free. By applying the Thermodynamic State-Space Model (TSSM) as a normative computational phenomenology grounded in Karl Friston’s Free Energy Principle (FEP) and neuroeconomic theories of cognitive control, we resolve both errors. Within a bounded physical system, an epistemic subject is separated from external states by a Markov blanket that precludes empirical verification of any extra-systemic utility. Furthermore, sustained deliberation over unfalsifiable metaphysical claims imposes severe neuro-computational opportunity costs on frontoparietal control networks, particularly the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC). Once cumulative processing demands breach a critical executive threshold (C_crit), the cognitive architecture undergoes a non-linear dogmatic phase collapse, driving system temperature (τ)—a formal measure of cognitive exploratory variance and stochastic policy flexibility to its functional floor (τ_min = 0.01) to preserve resource homeostasis. Through this lens, Epicurean tranquility (ataraxia) is revealed not merely as a philosophical virtue, but as a precise neuro-energetic conservation strategy.

items.title: From Emotions to Atmospheres.
Boredom as an architectural syndrome.
It (only?) looks like trouble.
items.abstract: ‘It looks like p’ generally leads to the inference that p is likely true. ‘It only looks like p’ generally leads to the inference that p is false. I explore this contrast, which is surprising from the point of view of theories of implicature and ‘only’.

items.title: Herman Cappelen, The Concept of Democracy: An Essay on Conceptual Amelioration and Abandonment, Oxford University Press, 2023, 244pp. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Mahmoud, Marwan. "The Concept of Democracy: An Essay on Conceptual Amelioration and Abandonment by Herman Cappelen." Tabayyun 15, no. 58 (Autumn 2026): 165-176.

items.title: Under the Conceptual Hood of Trustworthy AI: Reverse-Engineering the Moral Drivers of the Trust Debate.
items.pub: In Manuel Gustavo Isaac, Lily E. Frank & Jeroen Hopster, Reshaping the world: Conceptual engineering for emerging science and technologies. Wiley.
items.venue: Reshaping the world: Conceptual engineering for emerging science and technologies
items.abstract: The notion of “trustworthy AI” occupies a central place in contemporary debates on AI ethics, regulation, and governance, yet its conceptual foundations remain contested. Much of the discussion focuses on whether trust and trustworthiness—traditionally understood as interpersonal and moral concepts—can be meaningfully applied to technological systems. This article takes a different approach.
