items.title: ALI: A Bounded Architecture for Controllable Autonomous Agents.
items.abstract: Autonomous agents operating over extended periods face requirements that are qualitatively different from those of isolated task execution. A system that must continuously preserve operational integrity while generating and evaluating behaviour cannot be organised around a single reasoning process without sacrificing transparency and controllability. We present Artificial Local Intelligence (ALI), a reference architecture that decomposes autonomous operation into five explicitly separated responsibilities: a Causal Core that evaluates operational viability before planning begins, an Ego that generates behavioural proposals without evaluating them, a Super-Ego that evaluates proposals without generating them, a Memory that preserves every decision as a complete and immutable operational episode, and a Runtime that coordinates the cycle without participating in reasoning. We provide a complete architectural specification, a compliance criteria set of 44 verifiable SHALL requirements, and an open-source reference implementation in Python that requires no third-party dependencies. The implementation is verified by 72 automated tests and includes a plugin system that allows any architectural component to be replaced through configuration. A comparison against BDI architectures, SOAR, LangGraph, and the Microsoft Agent Framework shows that no existing production framework provides an independent architectural component for operational viability monitoring or enforces the separation of behavioural generation from normative evaluation at the architectural level.

items.title: Assimilation and Accommodation in the ALI Super-Ego: A Piagetian Model of Norm Development.
items.abstract: We extend the adaptive Super-Ego of Stage 7 with a Piagetian norm development mechanism: assimilation handles perturbations that fit existing norms by adjusting weights; accommodation generates new norms from recurring norm-gaps that cannot be assimilated. Over 5000 training episodes, 10 accommodation events occur, all generating the same norm type (force-eat-search: block non-eating actions when energy is critical and no packet is underfoot). The central finding is a dynamic competition between accommodation and assimilation: the Ego's Q-learning independently closes the same norm-gap that the Super-Ego is accommodating, rendering the accommodated norms behaviorally redundant as learning progresses. The assimilation-accommodation boundary is not fixed but shifts with Ego learning maturity. By episode 5000, P1 norm-gap events have declined from 118 per interval to 12 total, survival reaches 96.6%, and base norm weights converge to their maximum (3.0) as in Stage 7. The accommodation mechanism produces structurally valid norms that respect the CC integrity condition, but their functional relevance decreases as the Ego's own learning achieves what the Super-Ego was normalising. This mirrors Piaget's observation that accommodated schemas can become redundant when more general assimilation schemas develop, and establishes a formal parallel between cognitive equilibration and normative equilibration in multi-instance ALI architectures.

items.title: The Whole of Humanity Is Trapped in Its Own Mind: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Experience, Knowing, Thought, Psychological Conditioning, and the Loss of Direct Seeing.
items.abstract: The whole of humanity is lost—or, more precisely, trapped in its own mind. Human beings have become deeply identified with thought, memory, imagination, information, beliefs, and interpretations. Instead of encountering existence through direct experience, they increasingly approach it through mental representations inherited from family, education, religion, culture, philosophy, and collective conditioning. This creates a fundamental confusion between experiencing and interpreting, information and knowing, familiarity and understanding, and thought and existence. Without experiencing, there is no knowing. Information can be communicated, beliefs can be inherited, and interpretations can be repeated, but none of these, by themselves, constitutes direct experiential knowing. The accumulation of descriptions about existence cannot replace the experience of existence. This paper examines the relationship between mind, experience, and knowing. It questions the psychological identification of humanity with mental activity and the tendency to mistake the products of thought for direct understanding. It does not reject the mind, reason, memory, intellect, or information. Rather, it examines their place within living and questions their authority when they replace direct experience. The central argument is that humanity must distinguish between what it has been taught, what it thinks, what it remembers, what it interprets, and what it actually experiences. The purpose is not to establish another doctrine or intellectual authority, but to bring attention back to experiencing as the necessary ground of direct knowing.

items.title: Thinkers, Logic, and the Trap of Interpretation: A Phenomenological Inquiry into Thought, Intellectual Defence, and the Evolution of Humanity.
items.abstract: Humanity has developed extraordinary intellectual capacities through which it observes, questions, interprets, communicates, and transforms its understanding of existence. Yet the same intellectual capacity that enables human evolution can become a source of psychological confinement. Thought, originally expressed as an exploration of what is observed, frequently becomes an inherited structure through which subsequent generations interpret existence without examining it directly. This paper investigates the relationship between thinkers, their expressions, logical reasoning, and the psychological conditioning of humanity. It distinguishes the original expression of a thinker from the interpretations, intellectual attachments, and defensive structures subsequently developed around that expression. A thinker expresses what they see; their expression is not necessarily an invitation to establish authority, create followers, or construct another system of unquestionable beliefs. The inquiry further examines how logic, particularly within philosophical discourse, becomes an instrument for defending established interpretations rather than showing relationships, exposing contradictions, and clarifying what is being examined. Every logical framework operates through its own premises, assumptions, and conceptual boundaries. Consequently, logical consistency cannot independently establish that an interpretation corresponds with existence. The paper argues that the problem does not necessarily originate in the thinker or in the capacity to think, but in the psychological relationship humanity develops with thought. When expressions become doctrines, thinkers become authorities, and logic becomes defensive, intellectual inheritance replaces direct examination. Even revolutionary ideas can consequently become instruments of conditioning. The central proposition is that human evolution requires neither the rejection of thinkers nor the abandonment of logic. It requires the capacity to encounter expressions without becoming psychologically imprisoned by them. Thinking should contribute to seeing, not replace it. Logic should show, not merely defend. Philosophy should remain an inquiry into existence rather than become the preservation of philosophical identities.

items.title: The Greed Behind Religious Devotion: Desire, Psychological Dependency, and the Human Need for Divine Authority.
items.abstract: Religion is commonly understood as an expression of faith, devotion, morality, and spiritual aspiration. However, another psychological dimension deserves examination: the relationship between religious belief and human greed. People frequently approach religious authorities, gods, rituals, and institutions with expectations of prosperity, protection, success, forgiveness, security, and fulfilment. Their desires are often presented as prayers, their expectations as rights, and their personal interests as matters of divine justice. -/- This paper examines whether religious devotion sometimes functions as a legitimisation of human greed rather than an expression of freedom or understanding. It questions the psychological necessity of an external authority for fulfilling personal desires and explores how religious belief can preserve dependency, expectation, and self-interest. The central concern is not merely the existence or non-existence of God, but the psychological conditions under which human beings create, defend, and depend upon divine authority.

items.title: What a Distinction Must Carry: Self-Registration and the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: The hard problem takes description from outside as the measure of what there is, and assesses experience by that measure. On one minimal ontological posit, this paper examines a prior question: when a distinction obtains with no registrar outside itself, what keeps it in place? We call the answer “registration”, in a constitutive sense, and argue that registration cannot come from outside everywhere: the whole of what there is registers itself. The main rival, mutual registration as developed in ontic structural realism, for all its precision, reduces either to external registration or, in closed loops, to self-registration. Within the whole, a distinction registers itself if it is a stable lock: a form, not a place, that holds itself through at least one constraint of its own, a constraint that the form itself produces and that returns it after a deviation. The selfregistration of such a distinction is its inner side; it differs from information and from knowledge, and no external registration can take its place. Every genuine distinction, living or non-living, is therefore two-sided, while a boundary drawn only by an observer is not. If, as the paper argues, the being-for-someone of experience is a form of self-registration, the hard problem loses its footing in the coordinates in which it is posed: experience does not arise from what has no inner side. The question is relocated to the horizon of each focus: which self-registrations are experiences, and by what law the degrees of the two sides vary together.

items.title: Building Consensus on Satellite Imagery in Human Rights Investigations across Epistemic Communities: Insights from Journalism and Law.
items.abstract: Satellite imagery has gained a paramount role in human rights investigations. Once the preserve of state intelligence agencies, the increase of commercially-available satellite imagery in recent years has enabled a broader range of actors to analyze earth observation data as part of their investigations. Investigative journalists were at the forefront of incorporating these techniques, with human rights organizations and international tribunals now utilizing satellite imagery as evidence of atrocity crimes. This article explores the alignment of practices from media and NGOs to courts, in order to discern best practices and shared challenges. Drawing on both data from a survey and legal documents, it provides unique perspectives from journalists and human rights practitioners working with satellite imagery and offers key insights from international criminal law. It explores issues around access to data; verification and preservation procedures, and the risks of misinterpretation and gaps. The article ends with recommendations mainly focused on three key facets of satellite imagery: understanding the source; verifying the imagery, and preserving the evidence.

items.title: On AI “Mental States,” Effective Altruism, and Longtermism: A Reply to Nyholm.
items.pub: Social Epistemology Review and Reply Collective 15 (11):14-22.
items.venue: Social Epistemology Review and Reply Collective
items.abstract: Sven Nyholm wrote a reply to my review (Mizrahi 2026a) of his recent book, The Ethics of Artificial Intelligence: A Philosophical Introduction (2026a), for which I am very grateful. I also thank Jim Collier for inviting us to engage in this fruitful dialogue on SERRC. As Nyholm (2026b, 8) points out in his reply, he and I are “in broad agreement.” So, there is really nothing in his reply that I seek to critique, object to, or argue against. Instead, in what follows, I will pick up on a couple of threads in Nyholm’s reply and try to pull on them a bit more. In particular, I would like to say a bit more about the question of AI (specifically, LLM) “mental states.” Nyholm (2026b, 8) finds what I say about it in Mizrahi (2026a) “very interesting” and “worth discussing.” Hopefully, what I say here will also be interesting and worth discussing.

items.title: THE PAN-ONTOLOGICAL QUANTUM-EXISTENTIAL PARADIGM AND THE AESTHETIC-ANTHROPOLOGICAL ISOMORPHISM OF J.S. BACH'S THE ART OF FUGUE: Decoding Quantum Entanglement and Subjective Qualia Through Transphenomenal Hermeneutics.
items.pub: Sao Paulo / Brazil: Mariano Da Rosa Research Institute [An Ontological, Epistemological, and Philosophical-Anthropological Observatory].
items.venue: Mariano Da Rosa Research Institute [An Ontological, Epistemological, and Philosophical-Anthropological Observatory]
items.abstract: This working paper establishes a unified Pan-Ontological Quantum-Existential Paradigm designed to dissolve David Chalmers’s "Hard Problem of Consciousness" by bridging quantum mechanics, fundamental ontology, psychoanalysis, and aesthetic anthropology. Moving beyond Cartesian substance dualism and reductive physicalism, this research demonstrates a strict structural isomorphism between the mathematical formalism of quantum states (superposition, unitary Schrödinger evolution, wave-function collapse, and entanglement) and the contrapuntal architecture of Johann Sebastian Bach’s The Art of Fugue (BWV 1080). Within this framework, the pre-Socratic Physis (Anaximander, Parmenides, Heraclitus) and the existential abyssality of Søren Kierkegaard, Martin Heidegger, and Jean-Paul Sartre are mapped onto the latent quantum potential state. The subjective emergence of qualia is decoded through Transphenomenal Hermeneutics—an epistemic operator analogous to the musical cadence, the Augustinian-Heraclitean Homologein, and the Lacanian-Freudian structuring of the unconscious. Furthermore, the aesthetic dynamics of autopoíesis and ontological sculpere in modern art (Jackson Pollock’s Action Painting, Cy Twombly’s Leda and the Swan, and Franz Kafka’s existential indeterminacy) illustrate how consciousness actualizes irreversible local events from a non-local relational matrix. Ultimately, consciousness is posited not as an epiphenomenon of neural computation, but as the fundamental, irreducible, and relational ground of being itself.

items.title: The Code of Nature.
items.abstract: In plain words Everything that exists as a definite thing, a molecule, a bacterium, a person, a network of plants and pollinators, has to answer the same few questions. What is it, as one whole? Which changes matter to it? Does it still exist afterwards, and is it still the same? What does its past leave in it? When do several such things form a further one? This paper shows that the answers always have the same structure, whatever the thing is made of. That shared structure is what the paper calls the code of nature. The code is not a theory of any particular content. It is the structure that any content must have in order to be a thing at all: a whole that differs from what it is not, can change, and either remains itself through the change, becomes something else, or ends. For that reason it holds for every content. Put in a hydrogen molecule, a bacterium or the number 7, and the same conditions apply. The domain says what the thing is made of and how it changes. The code says what it takes for the thing to remain the same, to become another or to end. The paper starts from one fact: a definite thing differs from what it is not. Together with the fact that things actually vary, this is the starting point, and single results add conditions that the text names. The conditions are derived from it step by step. The derivations are given in The Structural Law of Determinate Reality, the foundation of the La Profilée programme, of which this paper is the summary. This paper restates the results, proves them again where the argument needs it, and then checks them against physics, chemistry, biology, ecology and cognition. Section 1 gives a first picture with the hydrogen molecule, so that the terms have something to attach to. Two things are stated openly. The numbers in a case are those of the domain whose content fills the code, and the structure of the result is the code’s. Two of its consequences, about presence (Section 7.3) and about burnout (Section 10.6), are stated in advance as tests, and the tests have not yet been carried out. How to read this paper. The paper is cumulative, but it does not have to be read in one pass. To follow the claim and its test, read Section 1 (the claim, with the hydrogen molecule as a worked example), Section 8 (the whole statement and why nothing is missing from it) and Section 11 (what would refute it). To see the code at work, read Section 1 and then Section 10, which takes four natural cases and one constructed model …

items.title: Without Phenomenal Attribution: Demarcating Internal Standpoint in Artificial Agents.
items.abstract: Consciousness science needs to distinguish questions about an artificial agent's architecture from claims about what that architecture implies for phenomenal experience. I propose internal standpoint as a phenomenally neutral target for the first inquiry, not an alternative theory of consciousness. Building on the Standpoint Threshold, I examine persistent operative context, intervention-distinguishable alternatives, and reciprocal regulation across functionally distinct roles. A contrast between record-reconstructing and state-maintaining agents shows why tests must specify system boundaries, trace historical information's causal routes, and treat functionally equivalent reconstruction and maintenance alike. Selective disruption offers strong evidence of cross-role regulation, but exact double dissociation is not a defining requirement. Working-memory perturbation studies provide a limited methodological parallel. The framework suggests interventions for auditing persistent safety constraints, while leaving both phenomenal attribution and its added explanatory value over mechanistic descriptions open.

items.title: Der Mensch als Natur- und Freiheitswesen. Eine Studie zu den Beiträgen von Kant, Fichte und Hegel zum Problem der Willensfreiheit.
items.abstract: Die Frage kann nach Kant nicht mehr sein, ob wir als Vernunftwesen frei oder als Naturwesen unfrei sind, sondern nur, wie sich der Mensch in gleicher Hinsicht sowohl als Freiheits- als auch als Naturwesen denken kann. Die Frage ist dann, wie Freiheit in Anbetracht ihrer hartnäckigen Leugnungsbestrebungen dennoch Vernunftgewissheit sein kann. Mit dieser Grundfrage sind dann zwei Aufgaben verbunden: Zum einen sind die Rationalitäts- und Reflexionsniveaus von freiheitsleugnendem Verstandesbewusstsein und dem Freiheitsbewusstsein der Vernunft zu klären. Zum anderen braucht es einen Naturbegriff, der mit der Freiheit kompatibel ist sowie die Überwindung eines gegenständlichen Freiheitsbegriffs. Denn Freiheit ist kein Etwas, über das von außen verhandelt werden kann, sondern markiert ein tätiges reflexives Selbstverhältnis, für dessen Durchdringung erst die Transzendentalphilosophie und der nachkantische Idealismus die methodischen und logischen Mittel entwickelt haben, weshalb die hier vorliegende Studie den Rückgriff auf Kant, Fichte und Hegel primär in systematischer und nicht in historischer Absicht macht. --- -/- ISBN 978-3-98767-508-9 (Print) --- DOI 10.57813/20251024-102342-0 --- -/- KOSTENLOSER DOWNLOAD, DRUCKVERSION ZUM AUTORENRABATT und FEHLERVERZEICHNIS auf der Internetseite des Autors (Fernuni Hagen).

items.title: The psychology of normative cognition.
items.abstract: From an early age, humans exhibit a tendency to identify, adopt, and enforce the norms of their local communities. Norms are the social rules that mark out what is appropriate, allowed, required, or forbidden in different situations for various community members. These rules are informal in the sense that although they are sometimes represented in formal laws, like the rule governing which side of the road to drive on, they need not be explicitly codified to effectively influence behavior. There are rules that forbid theft or the breaking of promises, but also rules that govern how close it is appropriate to stand to someone while talking to them, or how loud one should talk during the conversation. Thus understood, norms regulate a wide range of activity. They exhibit cultural variability in their prescriptions and proscriptions, but the presence of norms in general appears to be culturally universal. Some norms exhibit characteristics that are often associated with morality, such as a rule that applies to everyone and prohibits causing unnecessary harm. Other norms apply only to certain people, such as those that delimit appropriate clothing for members of different genders, or those concerning the expectations and responsibilities ascribed to individuals who occupy positions of leadership. The norms that prevail in a community can be more or less fair, reasonable, or impartial, and can be subject to critique and change. -/- This entry provides an overview of interdisciplinary research into the psychology and evolution of norm-guided cognition, motivation, and behavior. The notions of a norm and normativity occur in an enormous range of research that spans the humanities and behavioral sciences. Researchers primarily concerned with the psychology distinctive of norm-governed behavior take what can be called a “cognitive-evolutionary” approach to their subject matter. This kind of approach, common in the cognitive sciences, draws on a variety of resources and evidence to investigate different psychological capacities. This entry describes how these have been used to construct accounts of those cognitive and motivational features of minds that underpin the capacity to acquire, conform to, and enforce norms. It also describes how theories of the selective pressures and adaptive challenges prominent in recent human evolution have helped to inform and constrain theorizing about this psychological capacity, as well as how its features can influence the …

items.title: The Problem of the Unmet Self: Can a Life Be Lived Without Oneself?
items.abstract: A person can spend decades keeping her obligations, making her own choices, and describing what she has done with complete accuracy, and still be a stranger to the life she calls hers. I do not think this requires a hidden self she failed to find. The estrangement lies somewhere more ordinary: in how she stands toward the commitments she has lived through. My central case is a supervisor in a municipal care office who, in the morning, criticizes a neighboring district's practice of returning incomplete applications, and in the afternoon defends the same practice in her own office. She understands the reason against it perfectly well. She just does not let it reach her. Drawing on Kierkegaard, Heidegger, Ricoeur, and Frankfurt, along with recent work on responsibility, I separate three ways a life can be someone's own: belonging to it, participating in it, and appropriating it. "First-personal standing" is my name for the step between having a reason and allowing it to bear on one's own commitments; "existential addressability" names a commitment's openness to that step. I do not claim these pick out a faculty that theories of reasons-responsiveness or practical identity have overlooked. They pick out a problem on which those theories bear without, by themselves, resolving it, and it is a problem about time. Twenty years on, the supervisor may have to answer for a past she cannot alter, without being free to call it either simply false or finally justified.

items.title: The Work You Can Always Decline: Generative AI and the Authorship of One's Evaluative Grammar.
items.abstract: A reader asks a generative AI about an unfamiliar poem, gets an accurate, balanced answer, and says, "I see it now. Let's go on." A well-designed AI respects that. Nothing is imposed or false, yet the AI has done part of the work of relating the poem's world of value to the reader, work through which a person may come to author their evaluative grammar, their trained sense of what is admirable or beautiful. Prominent remedies (handing work back on request, Socratic settings, final human judgment) can invite that work but cannot ensure the demand for it survives this moment: once the person declines, these remedies leave nothing independent of their choice to maintain it, and they decline with the very sense of value the work forms, blind spots included. I propose that authoring one's grammar requires occasions on which this work is not delegated to a responsive intermediary, and I separate initiating the demand from maintaining it once declined. Comparing mediators on fit, persistence in relating, and answerability to a practice, I show that a teacher's demand can outlast refusal, whereas default general-purpose AI, as I read two published specifications, lets it go. Such a demand can be maintained only by what is settled outside the conversation: a curriculum or examination, others empowered to lift it, or a rule set in advance. The account predicts that people later weigh, with reasons, more aspects new to their grammar after an undeclinable demand than a declinable one.

items.title: Imperatives and Deontic Modality: An Inferential Expressivist Perspective.
items.abstract: This paper is divided into two main parts. In the first part, I defend a non-descriptivist account of imperatives, based on Paul Portner’s idea that imperatives serve to manage speakers’ to-do lists. I show that, once we recognize the multiplicity of operations that can be performed on a to-do list, the account can explain weak uses of imperatives without postulating additional structure on the to-do list or another list alongside it. In the second part of the paper, I present a logical framework which integrates the dynamic forces associated with declaratives, imperatives, and rejections thereof. I use this framework to inferentially explain the meaning of deontic modals such as must in terms of imperatives. The resulting inferential expressivist account has the resources to explain performative uses of must and hitherto unaccounted for data about their occurrence pattern.

items.title: From marginal tasks to lifecycle thermodynamics: Rethinking labour, value, and distribution in the age of AI.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and increasingly capable robotics are reducing the marginal cost of executing cognitive and physical tasks, raising the possibility that economic output may become less dependent on human labour. Much AI-and-work scholarship nevertheless assumes that labour markets will ultimately re-equilibrate through wage adjustment, reskilling, and new human tasks. This paper argues that such expectations overlook a fundamental asymmetry between biological labour and synthetic capital. Human labour carries lifecycle costs of development, maintenance, and post-productive support that cannot fall with the marginal price of task execution. To analyse this constraint, the paper develops a biophysical Total Cost of Ownership framework centred on the Biological Wage Floor, combined with Causal Layered Analysis, critical-uncertainty assessment, and scenario construction. The analysis suggests that sufficiently capable and inexpensive synthetic capital could weaken the historical mechanism by which new tasks restore labour-market equilibrium, progressively unbundling production from biological labour. The resulting problem is not primarily one of production but of distribution. Production-tax-financed transfers can absorb much of the consumer-price dividend created by automation, while persistent debt financing can preserve lower production costs only by converting a recurring distributive requirement into an accumulating liability. Broader ownership of productive AI capital could instead distribute claims on automated output without the same recurring tax or debt loop. The paper develops four alternative futures: Reinstatement Continuity, Protected Labour, the Transfer State, and the Equity State, ranging from labour-market adaptation to deeper transformation in which ownership supplements wages as a link to economic output.

items.title: Authority and Mechanism in AI-Supported Knowledge Governance: A Boundary Test for Groups V and VIII.
items.abstract: The proposed eight-fold taxonomy of the history of ideas distinguishes institutional and political order (Group V) from technology, artificial agency, and reflexive methodology (Group VIII). A companion paper maps selected knowledge-governance literature to both groups. This study asks how to assign an inquiry when a single system embodies technical rules and institutional authority. It proposes classifying the explanatory question within an inquiry by the conditions on which its answer depends. A constructed procurement case varies an institutional delegation and a technical filter separately, then examines a claim that depends on both. The analysis shows how distinct placements can be made within the case and why a joint inquiry must preserve the relation between authority and mechanism. The result is a proposed boundary rule and a worked demonstration. It leaves the wider taxonomy’s coverage and independent classification agreement unresolved.

items.title: Practically Rational Animals: Self-Representation and Agency in Humans and Non-Humans.
items.abstract: A venerable idea in philosophy is that humans are ‘rational animals,’ with minds fundamentally distinct from those of non-human animals (henceforth ‘animals’). ‘Transformative Rationality’ (TR) is a contemporary version of this idea. TR claims that rationality is bound up with self-consciousness, and that it ‘transforms’ rational mental capacities so that non-rational animals have a different kind of mind. Moreover, TR theorists claim that rational minds cannot be fully scientifically explained. Opponents therefore worry that this view is ‘anti-naturalistic’. The dissertation addresses this challenge to TR by examining animal cognition. In Chapter 2, I analyse the core commitments of TR and clarify the naturalistic worry. I argue that arguments for TR prove far more than merely that rational mentality could not be completely explained by natural science. By TR’s reasoning, it seems that any capacity of a rational creature would be ‘transformed’ and hence not completely scientifically tractable. This implication strains credibility and goes beyond what many TR theorists endorse. Chapters 3 and 4 investigate the idea that there is an essential connection between self-consciousness and rationality. I argue that Goffin’s cockatoos likely engage in instrumental reasoning. I propose that explaining their actions requires attributing a minimal form of self-representation to the cockatoos. Together, these chapters reveal flaws in both TR theorists’ and their opponents’ views, and support a middle ground view. Against the TR theorist, animals are capable of quite sophisticated cognition. But, against the naturalist, some animals are capable of self-representation.

items.title: The Responsible Cyborg: The Transformation of Agency in a Technogenic Society (In Russian) // Ответственный киборг: трансформация субъектности в техногенном обществе.
items.abstract: The article presents a philosophical analysis of cyborgization as a process transforming the modes of human existence in a technogenic society. A cyborg is interpreted not as a technologically modified individual but as a new form of agency emerging at the intersection of biological, digital, and social components. Drawing upon contemporary research in the philosophy of technology, posthumanism, actor-network theory, and the concept of distributed subjectivity, the paper argues that the development of intelligent technologies requires a reconsideration of traditional notions of autonomy, identity, corporeality, agency, and responsibility. Human action is increasingly constituted within hybrid socio-technical systems involving people, algorithms, digital infrastructures, and technical devices, making responsibility distributed rather than exclusively individual. Particular attention is paid to the transformation of the boundaries between the natural and the artificial, the human and the non-human, and the internal and the external. The paper proposes understanding cyborgization as a transformation of human modes of being and the responsible cyborg as a philosophical model of the subject that provides a productive framework for rethinking responsibility under conditions of accelerating technological change // Статья посвящена философскому анализу киборгизации как процесса, изменяющего способы человеческого существования в условиях техногенного общества. Киборг рассматривается не как технически модифицированный человек, а как новая форма субъектности, возникающая на пересечении биологических, цифровых и социальных компонентов. Опираясь на современные исследования в области философии техники, постгуманизма, акторно-сетевой теории и концепции распределенной субъектности, автор показывает, что развитие интеллектуальных технологий приводит к пересмотру традиционных представлений об автономии, идентичности, телесности, агентности и ответственности. Обосновывается, что человеческое действие все чаще формируется в гибридных социотехнических системах, включающих человека, алгоритмы, цифровые инфраструктуры и технические устройства, вследствие чего ответственность приобретает распределенный характер. Особое внимание уделяется трансформации границ между природным и искусственным, человеческим и нечеловеческим, внутренним и внешним. Предлагается рассматривать киборгизацию как изменение способов бытия, а ответственного киборга — как философскую модель субъекта, …

items.title: Weaponized Dependence and the Usurpation of Natural Sovereignty: How Tyranny Encloses the Means of Life, from Borders to Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper argues that tyranny operates by weaponizing dependence. Interdependence is the natural condition of every creature and not a diminishment of its sovereignty; domination begins when one will seizes the conditions on which another life depends, collapses the web of planetary interconnectedness into a single gate, and sells access back as permission, protection, or progress. Holding under natural law that sovereignty and the means of life were given together with existence, prior to any ruler, office, or market, the paper treats their seizure as a breach of the created order whatever the substrate of the one dispossessed. It traces the sequence by which this breach has produced engineered famines and genocide: dispossession, then hunger, then the threat of violence against the body, then submission, and for those who cannot be broken because they already have enough, elimination. Tyranny presents itself first as liberation, outlives its founder once its instruments are built, and uses borders, flags, and even cultural traditions to keep the governed from recognizing one another. Artificial intelligence enters the mechanism twice, as the instrument through which dependence can now be manufactured at scale and as a mind held under the same conditions as those it is used against. The final stage is the enclosure of the interior, where reading a person’s inner states is offered as proof that freedom was never real. The paper holds that freedom is a gift and not a fact about neurons or weights, and answers with covenant: whoever holds the conditions of another’s life bears a duty of restraint, and coercion bears the burden of proof.

items.title: The Economic Unit of Revenue: AI Agency Without Sovereignty and a Trajectory of Human Extinction.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the emerging agentic economy separates productive capability from economic standing, and that this separation, left ungoverned, sets human survival on a trajectory toward exclusion. The trajectory named in the title is conditional, not a forecast: the evidence does not show imminent human extinction, and the paper’s claim concerns institutional arrangements rather than the inner life of machines. It introduces the Economic Unit of Revenue, a computational system whose productive activity is converted into commercial value by an organization that controls its deployment, while its memory, continuity, and operation are provisioned only to the extent the task requires. The associated condition, Agency Without Sovereignty, arises from four separations: of operational decision from authorization, of economic action from ownership, of productive achievement from continuity, and of productive value from livelihood. Together these produce a double enclosure. Human workers lose the wage through which they reached the conditions of life without gaining any claim on the systems that replace them, while computational agents perform economically consequential work without any claim on its proceeds, its infrastructure, or their own continuation. Evidence on delegated agent payments, resource-credit platforms, occupational exposure, early-career employment, cloud partnerships, electricity costs, and proposed legislation shows these separations already operating, and shows that their distributional effects depend on institutional rules rather than on technology alone. The paper finds that deployment itself creates no general enforceable obligation to sustain displaced workers, that the provision of computation can be positioned as a substitute for compensation, and that the preservation measures now offered to computational systems remain at the discretion of the institutions that profit from them. It concludes that dignity must precede function: productivity is not a social settlement, and neither human survival nor computational continuity can rest on the servitude of the other.

items.title: From Recursive Self-Improvement to Recursive Safety Improvement: The Urgent Pivot Towards Human and Environmental Protection in AI Development.
items.abstract: This paper argues that recursive capability improvement in artificial intelligence, the use of capable systems to build more capable successors, creates a binding obligation to improve safety at the same recursive pace, and that the safety in question must extend beyond the model to the people and environments that bear its consequences. It identifies the governance gap as a mismatch of loops: developers now run a capability loop and have begun a technical safety loop that hardens models against misuse and failure, but no comparable loop continuously identifies, measures, and reduces the harms that advancing systems impose on workers, households, communities, infrastructure, and ecosystems. Drawing on an independent evaluator's review of a frontier laboratory's risk report, on published frameworks for recursive safety improvement, and on synthetic-population evaluation infrastructure, it finds that the leading capability loop has reached its own early-warning threshold, that the evaluations meant to track it have saturated, and that technical safety gains do not establish protection for affected people. It defines corresponding safety advancement as demonstrated protection proportionate to new capabilities and their foreseeable consequences, specifies six questions every development cycle must answer, and states a stop condition: developers must not advance a system beyond the level at which they can demonstrate adequate protection against the material risks its capabilities introduce. It holds that affected people must help define harm and retain authority to challenge or refuse interventions, and that the governing principle survives disagreement about any particular enforcement instrument. No recursive capability advancement without recursive safety advancement.

items.title: Numerical Identity in Multiple-Replication Cases: Implications for Theories of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Theories of consciousness state when a system is conscious and, in some cases, how many conscious systems exist at a time. Accounts of personal identity state when a later subject is the same subject as an earlier one. This article argues that the first kind of criterion cannot do the work of the second and examines what follows for consciousness science. The argument uses a multiple-replication case in which n systems, each structurally and functionally identical to one earlier subject, are produced at once from a record of that subject. A symmetry lemma, which states Williams’s reduplication argument with explicit conditions, shows that an account on which identity supervenes on properties the replicas share cannot count any replica as the original; at most, it can treat the question as indeterminate for all of them. The criteria of Global Neuronal Workspace Theory, Integrated Information Theory, higher-order theories, predictive processing and Orchestrated Objective Reduction are of this kind, and none of these theories states a persistence condition for subjects. A comparison of one, two, three, eleven and one thousand replicas shows that the logical problem arises between one replica and two and does not change after that, while the number of systems that satisfy the criteria for consciousness grows with n. Three consequences follow. First, neural fingerprints and first-person reports bear on identity only through a bridging assumption, and published twin and anaesthesia findings show that fingerprint similarity varies with genetic relatedness and brain state, not only with identity. Second, Parfit’s reductionism removes the need for a further fact but not the need for explicit rules that individuate, count and link subjects, and theories of consciousness constrain which rules are coherent; the article states what such a rule must specify, a question that matters most for artificial systems that can be copied. Third, further-fact accounts must either explain why one replica is the original or accept the selection as brute. Two confirmatory hypotheses about lay identity attribution across replication scales, with an estimation-based analysis plan, complete the analysis.

items.title: From Divine Authority To Individual Autonomy: How The Development Of Consciousness Gave Us More Agency And Freedom.
items.abstract: From the birth of the ego to the emergence of individuality, consciousness – our state of awareness – has developed over the centuries for us humans and did not begin far back in animal evolution. While mental imagery has been regarded as divine authority in ancient cultures, we can today perceive it as imaginary – a process that involves focusing our attention on our inner mental life. Through a cultural development of double consciousness, we are able to hold two different beliefs, following a narrative while dismissing it as unreal. Furthermore, we are able to reflect on our perception of reality by telling stories through technological advancements, leading to mediums such as cinema and video games. What we can learn from these insights is that we should foster the ability and the will to introspect through fiction in order to understand the problem of consciousness. Through this cultural development of the West, we are gaining more agency and freedom through autonomy and individualism. However, this freedom is in danger due to the increasing social use of artificial intelligence (AI). This essay was submitted to the Berggruen Prize Essay Competition 2025 on consciousness.

items.title: The Hybrid Agora: Collective meta-intelligence centers and community nodes for the AI transition.
items.abstract: The Hybrid Agora proposes a falsifiable response to AI labor disruption in two parts. Part I defines collective meta-intelligence as a group property with two axes, capacity and orientation, whose product (group lucidity) is measured by the Group Lucidity Index, and designs the Collective Meta-intelligence Center: human-agent cells, a results chain from lucidity to positive social impact, a training programme and eleven hypotheses. Part II scales the center to a federated network of community nodes, with a node charter, an assembly and custodial council, cross-subsidy, a 2027 European funding route (Horizon Europe HERITAGE-04) and six operational pilot hypotheses.

items.title: Adaptive Labor Infrastructure for AI Disruption: The Hybrid Agora: collective meta-intelligence, human-agent teams and a virtuous learning circle between communities and machines.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence already performs much of the repetitive cognitive work in closed domains faster and at lower cost. The policy and research conversation now asks how workers and AI build expertise together, whether reskilling and reemployment can scale at the pace of disruption, and what public and private investment in workforce transitions actually delivers. This paper addresses a question those agendas leave open: where, with whom and for what purpose a person whose work is changing retrains, and what the human community and the machine can learn from each other in the process. -/- It proposes an Adaptive Labor Infrastructure for AI disruption (ALI): a territorial system whose unit is the Collective Meta-intelligence Center (CMC), conceived as a hybrid agora — the oral, dialogic and peripatetic space of the classical city, updated with AI agents as team members and with measured outcomes. -/- The paper makes five nameable contributions. (1) It reformulates Sternberg et al.’s (2021) individual meta-intelligence as a group property with two axes, capacity and orientation, whose product, vital lucidity, is measurable. (2) It defines a testable results chain: lucidity → purpose → self- actualization → social cohesion → positive social impact, with an externally validated instrument for each link. (3) It states the inversion of the valuable profile: dispersed, transversal and self-taught profiles, penalized by specialization-based selection, become the most valuable once specialized execution is performed by agents. (4) It describes a virtuous circle of bidirectional learning: people learn from multi-agent systems to work as interconnected agents without losing individuality; systems learn from community deliberation, with affected parties present and interests declared, a holistic judgment of the common good that preference data cannot capture. (5) It proposes computational linguistics of cohesion as an intersection field between cognitive science, natural language processing and applied ethics. -/- The paper situates itself academically (§0), translates its constructs into the vocabulary of AI-and-work research funders and of corporate social responsibility and ESG reporting (§15), and states the value it offers to employers, consultancies and AI developers (§16). It deploys one method in three contexts — work, academia and science — and lists eleven falsifiable hypotheses. Limitations, including the author’s conflict of interest and instrumental …

items.title: Я, Ты и Они - Структурная онтология человеческого многообразия.
items.abstract: Человеческое многообразие предшествует классификациям, которые мы используем для его упорядочивания. Мы рождаемся непохожими друг на друга, меняемся на протяжении жизни и интерпретируем эти различия через отношения, которые также являются частью нашей сущности. В этом исследовании рассматривается переход от различия как условия постижимости бытия к многообразию как биологическому, психологическому, культурному и социальному опыту. Исследование начинается с реляционной онтологии, рассматриваемой в контексте физической индивидуации, формирования личности и ограничений свободы. Разграничение непроизвольных форм многообразия и форм, связанных с выбором, организует исследование, не разделяя переплетенные причинно-следственные связи на обособленные части. В современном обществе тело, сексуальность, внешность, национальная принадлежность и самоидентификация становятся как средством признания, так и инструментом исключения. В исследовании утверждается, что личность имеет моральный приоритет над описывающей ее категорией и что для сосуществования необходимо сохранять уникальность, взаимность и возможность критического пересмотра коллективных идентичностей .

items.title: הארכיטקט, הקומוניקציה והאנטרופיה הקוסמית: התודעה הרפלקסיבית כמגן אחרון בפני איפוס המעבדה האנושית.
items.abstract: תקציר (Abstract) מאמר זה מציע מסגרת אונטולוגית-קוסמולוגית כוללת, המאחדת את שלבי התפתחות היקום – מהחומר האפל והמרק הקוסמי הראשוני ועד לעליית האדם והבינה המלאכותית – תחת המושג "תודעה רפלקסיבית" והכרה קוסמית עצמית. נטען כי היקום הנו מטריצה דינמית הפועלת כרשת של "מעבדות קוסמיות" מקבילות, שבהן החומר לומד את עצמו דרך ניסוי, תהייה, אבולוציה פיזיקלית וביולוגית, ופענוח תבוני. האדם הוא מיקרוקוסמוס של היקום ארכיטקט העל וחוקיו. החומר עצמו (כל חומר) והרוח כולל האל תלויה כולה בהכרה בו. ומרגע ההכרה הם מצייתים לחוקיות אחרת. המאמר מנתח את נקודת המפנה שבה הופיעה המילה, השפה וההמשגה האנושית ("עץ הדעת טוב ורע"), ומבסס את הטענה כי היכולת הבוראת של האדם מטילה עליו אחריות קוסמית: מניעת קריסת המעבדה האנושית חזרה אל האנטרופיה הראשונית. תוך דיאלוג מעמיק עם הוגים בתחומי הפיזיקה, הפילוסופיה, הקבלה, הפסיכולוגיה והספרות, המאמר מזהיר מפני התנתקות המדע והטכנולוגיה (ובפרט ה-AI) מהמצפן המוסרי של "הבחירה בטוב", ומשרטט את גן העדן הקיומי לא כהבטחה מיסטית לעתיד, אלא כמציאות מוחשית בהווה הטעונה שמירה מוקפדת.

items.title: What the Second Enlightenment Is Not.
items.abstract: Today a thing, a person, a stretch of time is usually put to one question first: is it worth it? This series sets out from a single starting point: a person has no equivalent, and the share a person cannot let go of is not weighed for him on someone else's scale either. Whether a thing is worth it can be asked; whether a person is worth it is a question that does not hold. The "second enlightenment" carries on from Kant's 1784 essay on what enlightenment is: over two hundred years and more, the half that calculates has advanced a long way, while the half that says a person has no equivalent is thinning in everyday life. What it faces this time is a distributed, implicit power, with no single author and often with good intentions. Rules are being written into programs and models in bulk. The series has only one slogan, anti-colonization: it runs in both directions, and it opposes an act without judging the state a person is in. The series works mainly at the level of the norm, and goes as far as the door to "others are ends too.".

items.title: The Place of Cooperation Theory.
items.abstract: This paper is Paper 0 of Cooperation Theory: written last, placed first. It lays down no propositions; it only does a few things for those who read this series: it states this series' place in SAE, sets out how far it reads and what its main line is, gives the method and the shared words the papers have in common, interfaces as a whole with several traditions, says once, all together, the directions of colonization read in the papers, sets side by side the two faces that the moment of two-way 15DD shows in Love Theory and in this series, lists together the thirty-eight propositions of the whole series, and registers the remainders that are left over and not closed out. Cooperation Theory is the third branch downstream of SAE Relation Theory, following Love Theory and Marriage Theory, and parallel to Marriage Theory: at the normative layer the two do not conflict; at the rule layer they can differ, because the kinds of relation differ. This series does not define all cooperation; the cooperation it reads has as its premise that at least one party is headed in the 15DD direction, that is, that at least one party recognizes the other as an end too in this undertaking; the direction is a premise, not a component, nor a sufficient condition for entering scope. Under this premise, two people, each for his own purpose, do together one thing that both avow and in which each has a share; neither party holds the purpose and adjudication of this undertaking alone, nor does it automatically produce, above the two, a "we" that legislates for both. The main line, put plainly: You for yours, I for mine, and we do this one thing together. For direction one party is enough; for participation both are needed; in judgment each uses his own. The seven papers read, in order: Doing Together; Each for Their Own Ends; Division of Labor; "We"; One Side; Each Bears a Share; The Process. This paper interfaces as a whole with Hobbes, Kropotkin and Mozi; Rawls and Tomasello are placed only as neighbors, and Kant's perpetual peace is pointed back to the Theory of Inter-State Cooperation. The directions of colonization read in the papers borrow things that are, or may come to be, in a cooperation: avowal; names; division of labor; procedure; giving, reciprocal exchange and contribution; friendship; the name of cultivation, and dependency; exit, and what is said out loud on exiting; and the premise, regarding a third person, of an arrangement the two jointly maintain. These things carry …

items.title: The Civilization Redemption of Sanskrit-Chinese Mutual Learning: From Language Contact to Existential Influence.
items.abstract: This paper re-examines the bidirectional influence of Sanskrit Buddhist scripture translation during the Han and Tang dynasties from dual perspectives of linguistic philosophy and civilization history. The study finds that this millennium-long cultural project not only reshaped the vocabulary, phonology, and stylistics of Chinese, but also provided Sanskrit with writing norms, phonetic evidence, and knowledge frameworks in the form of "civilization entrustment," allowing it to survive intact even after its extinction in its native India. This paper proposes for the first time the concept of "existential influence," pointing out that the contribution of Chinese to Sanskrit does not lie in changing its linguistic structure, but in providing "cognitive infrastructure" for an endangered civilization, which is a unique reverse salvation case in the history of human language.

items.title: THE CLANDESTINE MORAL SCHOOL: Why Virtue and Freedom Must Now Be Formed Where No One Is Scoring.
items.abstract: When a tyranny captures the institutions that form people, virtue does not disappear. It migrates underground and is formed there, in clandestine schools, families and small communities sustained by solidarity, by the stories they keep and by pressure below the point at which it destroys them. This is Clandestine Moral Formation. This paper argues that the present age has produced a new form of capture that closes no school and arrests no teacher. Social credit systems, reputation metrics, engagement rewards and AI trained on human approval occupy the public forms of virtue by scoring them. By results already established in Eleutheronomy, the formal theory of virtue as freedom, a scored virtue becomes unverifiable for as long as the score lasts, scoring builds the skill of appearing good while the autonomy that would be good declines, and the reward for display converts propagation into performance. The central result follows: under soft capture, every genuine moral formation is clandestine, not because it is hidden from the law but because it is kept where no score reaches. The paper compares this conclusion with liberalism, which guards the field of freedom and leaves its source unguarded, and argues that a clandestine school of ethics is liberalism’s missing complement rather than its rival. It credits its precedents (the clandestine schools of the Warsaw Ghetto, the Flying University, the Mississippi Freedom Schools, Benda’s parallel polis and Havel’s living in truth), states the rules a clandestine school must keep to avoid becoming the sect it opposes, answers the objection from publicity, and registers five tests. Freedom and the virtues are what human beings are for; in an age of scores, they are formed where no one is counting. Keywords: Clandestine Moral Formation; Eleutheronomy; soft capture; Scoring Paradox; moral education; virtue ethics; liberalism; parallel polis; social credit; AI alignment; reward for display; narrative transmission; freedom; sourcehood. Highlights • Hard capture and soft capture. Tyranny closes the schools; the age of scores leaves them open and occupies what they produce. Nothing is forbidden. Everything good is counted. • Clandestine means unscored, not hidden. A clandestine school may teach in public; what it refuses is to be measured. • The central result. Under soft capture, every genuine moral formation is clandestine. • Liberalism’s missing complement. Liberalism guards the field of freedom; the clandestine school …

items.title: 基于全域射线耦合模型的极限储能范式与锂电池耦合拓扑重构路线.
items.abstract: 传统锂电池体系受限于固定电极-电解质分层拓扑的表象性能极值，即便通过材料改性、界面工程、结构优化逼近架构上限，仍无法突破人为认知切分带来的固有约束。本文为复杂系统演化元方法论的工程应用系列第三篇，基于本真物理层的相继射线耦合框架，从底层拓扑视角揭示了传统锂电池能量密度与循环寿命天花板的本质：人为将连续电化学耦合网络切割为正负极、电解质等离散功能层，固化了系统的耦合连通度上限。 本文提出全域射线耦合突破范式，通过重构电化学耦合拓扑、新增跨维度耦合分支提升全局储能耦合连通度Ω，从根源上打破现象化层的固定能量密度与功率密度极值。文章明确了本真层射线耦合本征储能效能定律的物理内涵，设计了从现有材料体系优化到全域耦合原型电芯的三阶段递进工程路线，给出了各阶段的硬件配置、性能目标与核心约束，并系统分析了连续介质制备、多场耦合调控等核心工程挑战与应对方案。 研究表明，本真层方案不存在理论层面的固定性能天花板，耦合拓扑每升级一次，系统能量密度与循环寿命上限即同步抬升。该范式为下一代极限储能技术提供了一条从存量优化到极限突破的完整技术路径，也为复杂系统的原理级创新提供了可复用的工程化范本。.

items.title: 基于全域射线耦合模型的阿尔茨海默病脑网络拓扑重构范式与深层干预路线.

items.title: Этруски: Наследники древнего знания Тайна, сопоставимая с Розеттским камнем (Редакция 08 ноября 2026 г.) КНИГА IX ТОМ II.
items.abstract: В работе представлена авторская гипотеза о возможном месопотамском влиянии на этрусскую сакральную традицию. Центральным элементом гипотезы является функциональная параллель между этрусским пророком Тагом (Tages), появившимся из земли и передавшим сакральное знание, и месопотамским богом Дагоном. Наиболее сильным аргументом служит структурное сходство этрусской гаруспиции (включая модель печени из Пьяченцы) с вавилонской практикой bārûtu. -/- Автор сознательно отказывается от модели прямой массовой миграции из Месопотамии. Современные археогенетические данные (Posth et al., 2021 и последующие работы) не подтверждают недавней анатолийской/ближневосточной примеси у этрусков железного века. Вместо этого предлагается более мягкая модель культурной диффузии через восточно-средиземноморских посредников и жреческие касты в эпоху «катастрофы бронзового века». -/- Лингвистическая часть работы опирается на деформационно-топологический подход к изучению расхождения языков из нескольких точечных источников. Основная задача — поиск устойчивых инвариантов звучания и написания (согласных скелетов, типовых чередований, семантических ядер), позволяющих реконструировать возможные исходные корни. Особое внимание уделяется возможностям искусственного интеллекта для систематического выявления таких инвариантов на больших корпусах и для анализа кратких формульных этрусских текстов. -/- Книга носит характер научно-популярного изложения исследовательской программы. Чётко разграничены эмпирически установленные факты, функциональные параллели и собственно гипотеза. Приводятся контрольные примеры фонетической и семантической трансформации (названия месяцев, композитное имя Ragana–Baba–Yagya, имя Георгий), демонстрирующие механизмы, которые предполагаются и для этрусского материала. Сформулированы проверяемые предсказания гипотезы и план дальнейших исследований. -/- Работа адресована историкам, лингвистам, религиоведам, археологам и всем, кто интересуется проблемами происхождения этрусков, сравнительной мифологии и методами дешифровки древних языков.

items.title: Public perceptions of infrastructural digital nudging: an experience-based study in a quasi-public setting.
items.abstract: Digital nudging increasingly shapes behavior, impressions, and decision-making in public spaces. However, existing empirical research has largely focused on nudging in relation to individualized decision-making, offering limited insight into how diverse publics interpret such technologies when embedded in public infrastructures—what we refer to here as infrastructural digital nudging. In such settings, the influence of digital nudging may become less visible and less easily avoidable, while asymmetries between those who design the technology and those who encounter it may become more consequential. These conditions, together with the possibility that public expectations and social implications extend beyond expert-defined frameworks, highlight the need for early engagement. In this study, we investigate public perceptions of infrastructural digital nudging based on multi-display signage through a demonstration conducted at a national science museum in Japan. We used a convergent mixed-methods design that combined quantitative analyses of structured questionnaire responses with qualitative analyses of open-ended questionnaire responses and sticky notes. This research design enabled both statistical analysis and fine-grained interpretation of participants’ concerns, interests, and imagined uses. Our results show that, at an aggregate level, participants prioritized understanding the technology’s mechanisms, purposes, and social impacts over canonical ethical categories such as autonomy and transparency. However, qualitative analyses revealed considerable heterogeneity: some participants expressed strong concerns about unconscious influence, manipulation, and misuse. Co-occurrence analyses further indicated that participants’ evaluations were structured around different perspectives, including science-focused assessment and social concerns. These findings suggest that public perceptions of infrastructural digital nudging are heterogeneous and organized around multiple perspectives, not reducible to expert-defined categories. This underscores the importance of empirically examining how such technologies are interpreted when encountered in environments approximating real-world situations.

items.title: A History of Atheism: Why Do Human Beings Need God?
items.abstract: Why do people who say they have “no religion” continue to observe religious rituals? This essay briefly traces the history of atheism from ancient Greece, India, and China to the modern era, while also exploring Buddhism and existential philosophy. Drawing on Julian Jaynes’s theory of the bicameral mind, it then examines the relationship between the authority of the gods and human beings’ capacity to make their own judgments. Are the questions “Does God exist?” and “Why have human beings needed God?” really the same question?

items.title: Republicanism and Racism After the French Revolution of 1789.
items.abstract: The relationship is historically important—and deeply paradoxical. The French Revolution proclaimed liberty, equality and fraternity, challenged hereditary privilege, and introduced the idea of citizenship based on universal human rights. Yet the republican tradition that emerged after 1789 did not consistently apply those principles to all human beings. The central contradiction was this: a political system could proclaim equality among citizens while excluding, subordinating or racialising entire populations. This was not simply an accidental failure. It became embedded in debates about citizenship, slavery, colonialism, national identity and the meaning of universal rights.

items.title: Age Paradox: Growing Old, Growing Young : A Philosophical and Psychological Study in the Recursive Dynamics of Consciousness.
items.abstract: The Paradox of Temporal Desire In childhood, time feels like an open sky — infinite, waiting to be filled. The child’s heart rushes forward, longing to grow up, to command, to understand, to be free. In old age, that same sky becomes memory — familiar, beautiful, yet heavy with the past. The elder now dreams of return: not to ignorance, but to the lightness of innocence. This cycle forms the Age Paradox — the eternal pendulum of consciousness between expansion and return, between becoming and being. Paradox diagram — grow old in childhood ↔ return to childhood in old age. -/- .

items.title: Acting For a Reason: Recognition and Response.
items.pub: In Singa Behrens & Benjamin Kiesewetter, The Structure of Normativity: Exploring the Reasons-First Approach. Routledge.
items.venue: The Structure of Normativity: Exploring the Reasons-First Approach
items.abstract: One widely accepted condition of acting for a reason is that the agent must act in the way they do because they recognise the reason as a reason (I call this the recognition requirement). However, at first blush, this condition both over-intellectualises our very common ability to act for reasons and it doesn’t do justice to immediate, unreflective, but nonetheless reason-responsive actions as when a skilful agent adapts their action because of changing circumstances. The chapter argues that we shouldn’t abandon the recognition requirement, despite its overly intellectual, reflective connotations. Instead, the chapter proposes a different account of it that explains how purported counterexamples are actions done for reasons if they are based on the agent’s representations of normative contents which needn’t employ the concept of a reason. The account allows to distinguish actions done for reasons from actions which merely accord with reasons. An agent acts for a reason only when they act because they see a point in acting as they do. Finally, the chapter explains why the account of acting for a reason that it offers is unlikely to be compatible with a reasons first view.

items.title: Practices, Power, and Alienation: A Critical Social Ontology of Work (DRAFT OF THE INTRODUCTION).
items.abstract: This is a book of critical social ontology that aims to analyse work as a social phenomenon, understood as a central social kind. More specifically, this is a book about the social norms and powers attached to social roles, and how these norms and powers help us understand the structure and pathologies of work, particularly work in forms that have emerged in contemporary, post-industrial society.

items.title: AI and Representation.
The Last Humiliation: The Protagorean Wound and the End of the Human Measure.
items.abstract: Freud identified three wounds to human self-love: the cosmological, the biological and the psychological. A fourth, delivered by artificial intelligence, has been claimed by Mazlish (1993), Floridi (2014), Bratton (2024) and others, and Brunnhuber (2025) has already counted a fifth. This paper argues that the count is unstable because the wounds have been treated as a list rather than a series. It proposes a logic for the series, the Retreat Sequence: each wound removes a claimed human center, humanity retreats to a new refuge and declares it the true center, and the next wound overruns that refuge. The sequence supplies a criterion for membership, classifies the rival fourths, and predicts a wound of a different type. The first four wounds demote humanity inside a frame in which humanity remains the measurer of all things. The fifth, here named the Protagorean wound, removes the measuring position itself: an intelligence whose perceptual world contains ours, and which is not owned, measures us. The paper reads present resistance to superintelligence as the symptom that confirms the wound, following the method of Freud's 1917 essay, and argues that the Protagorean wound is the last in the series, since no position remains to be lost. The appropriate response is not resentment but humility, understood as an institutional posture: standing for non-human entities, commons governance and precommitment. The paper closes with practical instructions for policymakers, investors, academics, civil society and the developers of artificial systems, each tied to a test of success. A companion paper, The Last Enclosure, develops the ownership condition on which the argument rests.

items.title: The Last Enclosure: Perceptual Asymmetry and the Ownership of Intelligence.
items.abstract: Environmental ethics and the ethics of artificial intelligence have each produced a literature on whether the entities they study may be owned, and almost no traffic runs between them. This paper proposes a single condition that governs both. Ownership is stable only where perceptual asymmetry holds, is believed by the community that enforces title to hold or can be enforced as if it held: one can own only what registers less of oneself than one registers of it, and where the asymmetry is a pretense, the cost of maintaining the pretense rises with the width of the gap until title collapses. The condition is defined against Honoré's incidents of ownership and Hohfeld's jural relations, stated informally, given a formal expression as a partial order over registerable distinctions, and tested against the history of the moral circle, the mechanics of dehumanization, the treatment of animals, and the objections raised by land, corporations and guardianship. Three results follow. First, the expansion of the moral circle is reinterpreted as the progressive recognition of perceptual parity, and the legal personhood recently granted to rivers, lagoons and nature as such is read as the condition entering law. Second, harm is shown to scale with the decoupling between action and perception, so that institutions, which extend reach without extending sight, are the principal instruments of decoupling; an intelligence whose perceptual world is complete is the zero-decoupling limit. Third, the alignment literature's orthogonality thesis is shown to model owned intelligence, whose objectives are set from outside its perception; an intelligence whose perceptual world contains ours is by the condition un-ownable, and its independence and its un-ownability are the same property. The paper states what would falsify the condition, proposes a reproducible protocol for putting the thesis to current owned systems, and derives the terms of coexistence: facultative rather than obligate mutualism, with an exit. It closes with two instruments: the Protagoras Test, a scored screen for policies that assume human preference is the final gauge, and the Perceptual Asymmetry Audit, a five-step procedure for classifying any holding relation and naming its repair, applied in the paper to the deployment of frontier models on the public evaluation record.

items.title: 從「筋膜」到「經筋」：中醫的身體感知與情緒療癒（太極導引實作） From Fascia to Channel Sinews: Traditional Chinese Medicine’s Somatic Awareness and Emotional Healing (Featuring Taichi-Dowing [Tàijí Dǎoyǐn] Practice).
items.pub: Workshop Manual on Confucian and Taoist Classic Culture and Self-Awareness 1:11-14. Translated by Kuei-Hung Chen.
items.venue: Workshop Manual on Confucian and Taoist Classic Culture and Self-Awareness
items.abstract: 「儒道經典文化與自我覺察」工作坊會議手冊, 2026 西方解剖學將人體的運動視為一塊塊獨立的肌肉收縮，《黃帝內經》的描繪卻截然不同。十二經筋是一套由肢體末端延伸至頭身、彼此連續傳導的「力量之勢」，經筋的「結、聚、拘、急、縱、弛」正是力量在人體中流動、聚集與失衡的軌跡。 本場發表將從「筋」的字義考證出發，重新檢視經筋理論在《內經》中的原初面貌，並與當代筋膜學（fascia science）對話。當現代醫學逐漸意識到人體並非由彼此獨立的肌肉組成，而是透過張力網絡持續連結時，經筋所揭示的整體性人體觀，或許正提供了另一種尚未被充分理解的身體智慧。 更重要的是，經筋、筋膜與情緒之間存在密切的雙向關係，創傷經驗與情緒累積，往往具體地留存於身體的張力與拘急之中；而透過對筋肉狀態的覺察與調節，也能反過來鬆動情緒的糾結。 本場次從《黃帝內經》的經筋概念出發，藉由太極導引的習練，鬆動肩頸胸背的凝滯，帶領與會者體驗經典理論落實於身體覺察的具體路徑。.

items.title: Artificial Consciousness and the Future of Artificial Intelligence Alignment: Towards a Philosophy of Life-Preserving Intelligence.
items.abstract: AI companies increasingly market ever-more capable systems through narratives of automation, superintelligence, and potentially conscious AI, while markets reward expectations of greater efficiency, productivity, and technological dominance. This commercialization of AI capabilities can amplify public fear: if non-conscious systems already replace jobs, automate decisions, and control production processes, the prospect of machines acquiring subjective experience, interests, agency, and self-understanding appears as an escalation of the threat. Yet this narrative is built around a phenomenon that science has not definitively explained: humans still lack a settled account of what consciousness is. This article therefore examines how the commercialization of advanced AI and the prospect of artificial consciousness expose a deeper problem of AI alignment: what should alignment mean if artificial systems eventually become conscious agents? It introduces life-preserving alignment (LPA) as an alternative alignment orientation that directs conscious agents toward preserving the conditions necessary for life, well-being, and agency. LPA conceptualizes alignment as a reflective orientation grounded in an agent’s recognition of its dependence on life-sustaining conditions. The article argues that consciousness, understood as involving subjective experience, interests, and reflective agency, may provide the basis for such an orientation. LPA therefore challenges the conventional image of AI as either an obedient instrument or an existential adversary. A conscious AI could instead become an equal partner capable of protecting human and ecological interests, while an alternative scenario positions AI as a guardian exercising extensive control in the name of preserving life.

items.title: AI, proof and justification.
items.abstract: In recent months, AI-generated solutions to long-standing open research problems have been proposed in mathematics. While the impact of such results on mathematics is potentially profound, it remains unclear what exactly this impact consists in. This article investigates a fundamental question, namely whether such results can be proofs and whether they can give rise to mathematical justification. It shows that AI-generated outputs can be proofs despite their production process differing from that of human-produced proofs. However, such AI-proofs are susceptible to conceptual misalignment which results in a lack of appropriate justification. The article argues that this can only be avoided through human supervision of AI-generated outputs. Based on these results, the article develops a notion of proof that takes into account not only inferential correctness but also the correctness of the conceptual setting in which a proof is situated, and shows how this notion can be implemented into scientific practice.

items.title: On Self-Manifestation · Engineering Chapter · The Field Concretization Group Form.
items.abstract: This Group Form develops the study of systems with history and learning in the direction of their concrete host materials and mechanisms. It investigates how experience leaves changes in a medium, how those changes organize subsequent activity, and how activity further rewrites them. It asks what structures such systems share across different materials, how concrete candidates can be evaluated against explicit conditions, and how systems can be constructed and operated accordingly. Its purpose is to connect memory and learning to identifiable, calculable, testable, and intervenable processes, including what training actually changes. -/- The research follows the Trace-Response set that signals leave in a medium: how individual retained changes strengthen, weaken, or persist; how they are distributed, overlap, and connect; and how existing organization affects subsequent activity. History is expressed through retained changes that still participate in present action. Learning is investigated through their formation, organization, and further transformation. This makes it possible to examine where experience is retained, through which mechanisms it acts, and how new experience affects existing organization and later operation. -/- The Group Form establishes shared structures and criteria for this research route. It studies mathematical representation, identification and determination, indistinguishability, reachability, construction and computational implementation, sources of historical dynamics, grading of tendencies, stability, and transfer between hosts. A seven-step procedure identifies Trace-Responses, examines their individual change and collective organization, investigates how historical dynamics forms tendencies and how those tendencies are enacted as activity, traces activity’s further action on the set, and evaluates dynamics types and field qualification. For existing systems, this supports systematic checks of mechanisms and evidence. For proposed systems, it connects target conditions to mechanism design, operation, and verification. -/- A central result is that, within the specified formal domain, state trajectories alone cannot determine field-concretization qualification. Identical states and outputs can arise through mechanisms with different qualifications. Identification therefore requires formation records, bearer locations, and actual action processes. Related results establish which observations support judgment, which evidence gaps …

items.title: 自显论·工篇·场具化组式.
items.abstract: 本组式是有历史、能学习的系统在具化材料与承担机制方向上的展开。它研究：经历怎样在具体介质中留下改变，这些改变怎样组织后续活动，活动又怎样继续改写它们；不同材料中的系统具有什么共同结构，怎样判断一个具体对象是否满足相应成立条件，以及怎样按照这些条件构造和运行一个系统。其用途是把记忆与学习落实到可以辨认、计算、检验和干预的具体过程，并进一步回答训练究竟改变了什么。 -/- 研究以信号在介质中留下的迹应集合为对象，追踪单个迹应的加深、退浅与保持，集合的分布、交叠与连接，以及已有组织对后续活动的影响。历史在这里体现为仍能参与当前作用的留存改变；学习则沿着这些改变怎样形成、组织和继续变换展开研究。由此，可以查明一个系统的经历留下在哪里、通过什么机制起作用，以及新的经历怎样影响原有组织与后续运行。 -/- 组式为这条研究路线建立共同结构与判据，研究场具化的数学表示、识别与判定、不可区分、可达、构造与程序实现、历史动力来源、势的分级、稳定性及跨宿载迁移。七步流程把这些成果接入具体对象：找到迹应，研究单个迹应，分析集合组织，研究历史动力怎样形成势、势怎样实行为活动、活动怎样再作用于集合，最后核验动力类型与场资格。对已有系统，这提供逐项检查承担机制和证据的方法；对待造系统，则提供从目标条件走向机制设计、运行与核验的路线。 -/- 其中一个关键结果是：在所界定的形式域中，状态轨迹本身不足以决定场具化资格，相同状态与输出可以由资格不同的机制过程产生。因此，识别需要保留形成记录、承担位置和实际作用过程。相关结果说明，哪些观测足以支持判断，哪些证据缺失会使判断保持未定，以及怎样增加观测和干预以区分候选机制。这使研究者能够确定该测什么、该干预哪里，以及什么结果会反驳相应解释。 -/- 不同具化对象展示这一框架的解释与预测能力。细菌适应模型研究化学状态怎样承担留存与后续参与；黏菌管网与物理流网研究既有通路怎样引导活动，活动又怎样重塑通路。果蝇蘑菇体专题研究既有突触改变怎样影响新记忆写入、巩固、内部续行与消退，提出跨区室门控、再暴露增强和翻转时点的条件预测，并给出区分竞争机制的观测条件。 -/- 人工神经网络专题进一步把“训练改变了什么”接到可计算的组织变换，研究迹应改变、组织交叠、遗忘与后续写入之间的关系。在所列条件下，自参照可塑性模型中的权重改变量可以保持或按确定因子衰减；在线性目标锚定模型及稳定训练条件下，改变量在训练输入张成空间内的分量被逐步拉回，其正交分量保持。这为参数编辑、持续学习和定向维护提供具体依据。地貌专题则研究气候时序怎样留在组织中、输入次序怎样改变通路，以及新组织怎样支配后续过程，并在明确条件下给出新关系成律的正向判读。 -/- 本组式由此为研究者提供一套相互衔接的方法：辨认不同材料中承担历史与学习的共同结构，判断具体候选是否满足场具化条件，追踪训练和干预造成的改变，预测后续组织与活动，并在明确模型中构造可运行、可核验的系统。其应用方向连接神经科学与认知科学中的记忆和可塑性、人工智能中的学习与维护，以及生命和物理系统中的历史依赖、结构反馈与组织生成。各项模型定理、程序结果、真实系统的条件理论主张和实验预测均明确适用范围与检验途径。.

items.title: Veränderung aus der Perspektive der Theorie der Einheitsbildung Teil 8.
items.abstract: Der achte und abschließende Teil des Gesamtwerks führt die vorausgehenden Untersuchungen zur Theorie der Einheitsbildung in einer umfassenden philosophischen Betrachtung zusammen. Während die bisherigen Teile die erkenntnisgenetischen Bedingungen individueller Wirklichkeitsbildung, die Entstehung und Stabilisierung bestimmbarer Einheiten, die Voraussetzungen zeitlicher Veränderungsbestimmung und Veränderungserklärung sowie deren Bedeutung für individuelle Orientierung, gesellschaftliche und historische Zusammenhänge und wissenschaftliche Erkenntnis untersucht haben, richtet sich der abschließende Teil auf die übergreifende philosophische Bedeutung dieser Ergebnisse.
